literature.headline_zh: 汉坦病毒本期文献呈现多方向研究进展
literature.lead_zh: 本期汉坦病毒研究集中呈现以下进展。
key_findings_zh: 与正常 IgG 不同,来自 DNA 疫苗接种受试者的人类抗体在两项实验中都提供了针对致命性 ANDV 攻击的显着保护作用。根据分析群体和模型参数,预测保护作用的探索性截止滴度确定为 PsVNA50 的 31-184 和 PRNT50 的 20-80。 [10.1016/j.ebiom.2026.106535]
对 MV Hondius 游轮上的 ANDV 传播 和之前的 暴发 的分析表明,气溶胶传播可能是在允许的环境条件下源病例和易感接触者之间 传播 的关键机制。 [10.1093/cid/ciag428]

news.headline_zh: 汉坦病毒本期公共卫生新闻动态
news.lead_zh: 本期汉坦病毒新闻集中呈现以下动态。
key_findings_zh: 亨特公共卫生医生克雷格·道尔顿 (Craig Dalton) 表示,一艘携带致命汉坦病毒菌株的游轮 暴发 不太可能成为下一次全球大流行。这是基于他对汉坦病毒行为和 传播 的专业知识和理解。 [news-b1d66a9505cb134d]
MV Hondius 号上的汉坦病毒暴发 导致 3 人死亡、6 人确诊感染以及其他疑似病例。世界卫生组织 (WHO) 于 2025 年 5 月 2 日标记了该群急性呼吸道疾病病例,疾病预防控制中心 (CDC) 将 暴发 列为 3 级紧急响应。 [news-67b72e1180b4a58e]
科学家利用冷冻电子显微镜揭示了安第斯山脉汉坦病毒如何识别并结合人类细胞受体 PCDH1,这对于病毒的进入和复制至关重要。 [news-2f9604a9a1e9f17f]
M/V Hondius 号游轮上发现了由安第斯山脉病毒引起的 暴发 或汉坦病毒感染。该事件得到了世界卫生组织的证实,该组织记录了 9 例疑似病例和 7 例确诊病例。社交媒体用户指出,这与 2012 年《辛普森一家》中的一集有相似之处,该集也以一艘感染病毒的游轮为主角。 [news-f9ee6341b8261248]
《生物学研究》杂志上发表的一篇评论讨论了针对安第斯病毒的抗体疗法,强调了中和和 Fc 介导的效应功能在 抗病毒药物 免疫和治疗功效中的作用。该事件已根据审查结果得到确认。 [news-6e547dcbe89e6eda]
news.trend_or_risk_zh: 风险判断仅依据入选来源已经确认的信息，不把媒体推测升级为官方结论。
news.lead_en: This reporting window highlights the following Hantaviruses news developments.
key_findings_en: Craig Dalton, a Hunter public health physician, stated that a cruise ship outbreak involving a deadly hantavirus strain is unlikely to become the next global pandemic. This is based on his expertise and understanding of hantavirus behavior and transmission. [news-b1d66a9505cb134d]

A hantavirus outbreak aboard the MV Hondius resulted in three deaths, six confirmed infections, and additional suspected cases. The World Health Organization (WHO) flagged the cluster of acute respiratory illness cases on May 2, 2025, and the CDC classified the outbreak as a Level 3 emergency response. [news-67b72e1180b4a58e]

Scientists used cryo-electron microscopy to reveal how the Andes hantavirus recognizes and binds to the human cell receptor PCDH1, which is critical for viral entry and replication. [news-2f9604a9a1e9f17f]

An outbreak of hantavirus infection, caused by the Andes virus, was detected on the cruise ship M/V Hondius. The event is confirmed by the World Health Organization, which recorded nine probable and seven confirmed cases. [news-f9ee6341b8261248]

A review published in the journal Biological Research discusses antibody therapies targeting the Andes virus, emphasizing the role of neutralization and Fc-mediated effector functions in antiviral immunity and therapeutic efficacy. The event is confirmed based on the review's findings. [news-6e547dcbe89e6eda]

papers.title: Evaluation of Andes virus vaccine-derived human antibody for protection in Syrian hamsters: a passive transfer study using phase 1 trial sera.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Andes virus (ANDV) causes severe hantavirus pulmonary syndrome and is uniquely capable of person-to-person transmission, with no licenced vaccines or therapeutics available. A Phase 1 trial (NCT03682107) demonstrated that an ANDV DNA vaccine targeting Gn/Gc envelope proteins elicits neutralising antibodies in humans. We evaluated whether these human antibodies protect against lethal disease in an animal model. METHODS: Day 197 sera from vaccinated human subjects were pooled, purified, and passively transferred to female Syrian hamsters one day prior to lethal ANDV challenge across two independent experiments. Controls included normal human IgG, PBS (negative controls), and SAB-400 (positive control). Neutralising antibody levels were quantified using pseudovirion neutralisation assays (PsVNA) and plaque reduction neutralisation tests (PRNT) to determine exploratory cutoff titres predicting survival. FINDINGS: Human antibodies from DNA-vaccinated subjects-unlike normal IgG-conferred significant protection against lethal ANDV challenge in both experiments. The exploratory cutoff titres predicting protection were determined to be 31-184 for PsVNA50 and 20-80 for PRNT50, depending on the analysis population and model parameters. INTERPRETATION: Vaccine-induced human antibodies are sufficient to protect against lethal ANDV infection in an established animal model. If confirmed, these results indicate that neutralising antibody titres could serve as a surrogate endpoint and correlate of protection for future hantavirus Gn/Gc-targeted vaccines. FUNDING: Defense Health Program and the National Institutes of Health (NIH).

papers.title: Integrated immunoinformatics and molecular dynamics approaches reveal a promising multi-epitope vaccine against hantavirus.
papers.abstract: UNLABELLED: Hantavirus is a rodent-borne zoonotic pathogen causing Hemorrhagic Fever with Renal Syndrome (HFRS) and Hantavirus Pulmonary Syndrome (HPS), with substantial global morbidity and mortality. No universally approved human vaccine exists, making a safe, effective vaccine a public health priority. An immunoinformatics strategy was used to design a multi-epitope vaccine construct (MEVC) targeting the glycoprotein precursor (GP_HANTL) of Hantaan orthohantavirus. Cytotoxic T lymphocyte (CTL), helper T lymphocyte (HTL), and B-cell epitopes were predicted and screened for antigenicity, immunogenicity, MHC-binding affinity, and population coverage. Selected epitopes were joined with EAAAK, AAY, GPGPG, and KK linkers and fused to a β-defensin adjuvant. The construct was evaluated by physicochemical characterization, structural modeling, molecular docking, molecular dynamics (MD) simulation, immune simulation, codon optimization, and in silico cloning. The final construct comprised 10 CTL, 10 HTL, and 5 B-cell epitopes, with 99.24% global population coverage. Structural validation showed 95% of residues in favored Ramachandran regions and an ERRAT score of 82. Molecular docking produced a favorable ClusPro score (- 1273.6) for the selected MEVC-TLR4 complex. Immune simulations predicted robust humoral and cellular responses, including elevated antibodies, memory B cells, and CTL/HTL activation. Codon optimization yielded a CAI of 0.94, supporting efficient Escherichia coli expression. A 100-ns MD simulation showed substantial conformational adaptation of the MEVC while TLR4 remained comparatively stable; accompanying Rg and SASA trends indicated that the MEVC adopted a more compact state during the trajectory. The proposed MEVC demonstrated favorable predicted immunogenicity, favorable structural characteristics, broad population coverage, and favorable expression characteristics. These findings support experimental validation and development of a preventive strategy against Hantavirus infection. SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION: The online version contains supplementary material available at https://doi.org/10.1007/s40203-026-00782-6.

analysis.summary_en: This study aimed to develop a safe and effective vaccine against hantavirus, which causes Hemorrhagic Fever with Renal Syndrome (HFRS) and Hantavirus Pulmonary Syndrome (HPS), with significant global health impacts. Using immunoinformatics, a multi-epitope vaccine construct (MEVC) was designed targeting the glycoprotein precursor of Hantaan orthohantavirus. The construct was evaluated through physicochemical characterization, structural modeling, molecular docking, molecular dynamics (MD) simulation, immune simulation, codon optimization, and in silico cloning. Results showed favorable structural validation, conformational adaptation of the MEVC, and robust predicted immune responses. The MEVC demonstrated broad population coverage and efficient expression. These findings support further experimental validation and development of a preventive strategy against hantavirus infection. The study's reliance on in silico methods limits the confidence in the results, but the comprehensive computational analysis provides strong evidence for the vaccine's potential.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 汉坦病毒 是一种啮齿类动物传播的人畜共患病原体,可引起 肾综合征出血热 (HFRS) 和 汉坦病毒肺综合征 (HPS),具有很高的全球发病率和 死亡率。目前尚不存在普遍批准的人类 疫苗,因此安全、有效的 疫苗 成为公共卫生优先事项。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 采用免疫信息学策略设计了针对汉坦正汉坦病毒糖蛋白前体(GP_HANTL)的多表位 疫苗 构建体(MEVC)。通过物理化学表征、结构建模、分子对接、分子动力学(MD)模拟、免疫模拟、密码子优化和计算机克隆对构建体进行评估。
elements_zh.methods: 预测并筛选细胞毒性 T 淋巴细胞 (CTL)、辅助 T 淋巴细胞 (HTL) 和 B 细胞表位的抗原性、免疫原性、MHC 结合亲和力和群体覆盖率。选定的表位与 EAAAK、AAY、GPPGG 和 KK 连接体连接,并与 β-防御素佐剂融合。进行 100 ns MD 模拟以评估构象适应性和稳定性。
elements_zh.main_results: 结构验证显示 95% 的残基位于有利的 Ramachandran 区域,ERRAT 得分为 82。100 ns MD 模拟显示 MEVC 的显着构象适应,而 TLR4 保持相对稳定;伴随的 Rg 和 SASA 趋势表明 MEVC 在轨迹过程中采用了更紧凑的状态。所提出的 MEVC 表现出良好的预测免疫原性、良好的结构特征、广泛的人群覆盖度和良好的表达特征。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 这些发现支持通过设计具有广泛人群覆盖率和良好免疫原性的多表位 疫苗 构建体来制定针对汉坦病毒感染的预防策略。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 结果为实验验证和开发针对汉坦病毒感染的 疫苗 奠定了基础,这可以通过降低发病率以及与 HFRS 和 HPS 相关的 死亡率 来显着改善公共卫生结果。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究基于计算机方法,不包括实验验证,这限制了研究结果的可信度。然而,考虑到所使用的综合计算方法,证据是强有力的。

papers.title: Early warning indicators for severe hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome
papers.abstract: Hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS) remains a significant public health concern, and early identification of severe cases is critical for improving outcomes. This review synthesizes recent advances in early warning indicators for severe HFRS. Clinically accessible indicators form the basis of early risk stratification. Key bedside signs such as high fever, severe gastrointestinal symptoms, altered mental status, and overt bleeding tendency, together with routine laboratory parameters including thrombocytopenia, leukocytosis, and elevated procalcitonin, have consistently shown robust predictive value for disease severity and mortality. Immunological markers provide mechanistic insight that also supports early identification of severe HFRS, as reflected by a core cytokine imbalance, impaired antigen-specific T- and B-cell responses, and aberrant activation of monocytes, neutrophils, and the complement system. Emerging biomarkers of endothelial barrier disruption, early renal tubular injury, oxidative stress, and metabolic dysregulation may further enhance predictive capacity. Despite these advances, challenges remain regarding external validation and clinical translation. Future research should focus on establishing standardized, multicenter-validated early warning systems to enable precise management of severe HFRS.

analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: Despite these advances, challenges remain regarding external validation and clinical translation of the identified indicators. The review highlights the need for further research to address these gaps and improve the reliability of early warning systems.

analysis.summary_en: This review explores early warning indicators for severe hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS), emphasizing the importance of clinically accessible signs and laboratory parameters in predicting disease severity and mortality. Immunological markers are also highlighted for their role in understanding the pathophysiology of severe HFRS. While significant progress has been made, the review identifies challenges in external validation and clinical translation. It calls for future research to develop standardized, multicenter-validated systems and to investigate emerging biomarkers that could improve early identification and management of severe HFRS.

elements_zh.scope_and_question: 此次审查的重点是确定严重 肾综合征出血热 (HFRS) 的早期预警指标,这是一种由 肾综合征出血热 引起的疾病。核心问题是如何改进重症病例的早期识别,以提高患者的治疗效果。
elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 该综述系统地综合了严重 HFRS 预警指标的最新进展。它包括该主题的总体概述,并讨论用于识别和验证这些指标的方法。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 高烧、严重胃肠道症状、精神状态改变和明显出血倾向等临床可及指标,以及血小板减少、白细胞增多和降钙素原升高等常规实验室参数,始终显示出对疾病严重程度和 死亡率 的强大预测价值。免疫学标记物还为严重 HFRS 的早期识别提供机制见解,因为它们反映了核心细胞因子失衡、抗原特异性 T 细胞和 B 细胞反应受损以及单核细胞、中性粒细胞和补体系统的异常激活。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 尽管取得了这些进展,但在已确定指标的外部验证和临床转化方面仍然存在挑战。该审查强调需要进一步研究来弥补这些差距并提高预警系统的可靠性。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 未来的研究应侧重于建立标准化、多中心验证的预警系统,以实现严重 HFRS 的精确管理。这包括探索内皮屏障破坏、早期肾小管损伤、氧化应激和代谢失调的新兴生物标志物,以进一步增强预测能力。

analysis_en.scope_and_question: The review focuses on identifying early warning indicators for severe hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS), a disease caused by hantaviruses. The central question is how to improve early identification of severe cases to enhance patient outcomes.
analysis_en.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review is a systematic synthesis of recent advances in early warning indicators for severe HFRS. It includes a general overview of the topic and discusses the methods used to identify and validate these indicators.
analysis_en.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Clinically accessible indicators such as high fever, severe gastrointestinal symptoms, altered mental status, and overt bleeding tendency, along with routine laboratory parameters like thrombocytopenia, leukocytosis, and elevated procalcitonin, consistently show robust predictive value for disease severity and mortality. Immunological markers also provide mechanistic insight into early identification of severe HFRS, as they reflect a core cytokine imbalance, impaired antigen-specific T- and B-cell responses, and aberrant activation of monocytes, neutrophils, and the complement system.
analysis_en.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: Despite these advances, challenges remain regarding external validation and clinical translation of the identified indicators. The review highlights the need for further research to address these gaps and improve the reliability of early warning systems.
analysis_en.research_and_practice_implications: Future research should focus on establishing standardized, multicenter-validated early warning systems to enable precise management of severe HFRS. This includes exploring emerging biomarkers of endothelial barrier disruption, early renal tubular injury, oxidative stress, and metabolic dysregulation to further enhance predictive capacity.

media_mentions.content: Abstract Hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS) remains a significant public health concern, and early identification of severe cases is critical for improving outcomes. This review synthesizes recent advances in early warning indicators for severe HFRS. Clinically accessible indicators form the basis of early risk stratification. Key bedside signs such as high fever, severe gastrointestinal symptoms, altered mental status, and overt bleeding tendency, together with routine laboratory parameters including thrombocytopenia, leukocytosis, and elevated procalcitonin, have consistently shown robust predictive value for disease severity and mortality. Immunological markers provide mechanistic insight that also supports early identification of severe HFRS, as reflected by a core cytokine imbalance, impaired antigen-specific T- and B-cell responses, and aberrant activation of monocytes, neutrophils, and the complement system. Emerging biomarkers of endothelial barrier disruption, early renal tubular injury, oxidative stress, and metabolic dysregulation may further enhance predictive capacity. Despite these advances, challenges remain regarding external validation and clinical translation. Future research should focus on establishing standardized, multicenter-validated early warning systems to enable precise management of severe HFRS. 1 Introduction Hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS) is an acute infectious disease caused by several Orthohantavirus species in the family Hantaviridae. Human infection usually occurs through inhalation of aerosolized virus from the excreta of infected rodents (). The main causative viral strains differ by geographic region. Hantaan virus (HTNV) and Seoul virus (SEOV) are major causes of HFRS in Asia. HTNV infection may be associated with case fatality rates of approximately 5%–15%, whereas SEOV infection is generally milder. Puumala virus (PUUV) predominates in Europe and generally causes a milder form known as nephropathia epidemica (NE), with a case fatality rate of 0.1% to 0.4%. Dobrava virus (DOBV), which circulates mainly in the Balkans and other parts of Europe, has been documented to cause more severe disease (–). China accounts for >90% of the global HFRS burden, with more than 1.62 million cases and nearly 47,000 deaths from 1950 to 2014 (). During 2014–2023, 91,388 total cases were reported, corresponding to an average annual incidence of 0.65/100,000 (). Hantaviruses enter host cells primarily by binding to β3 integrins on the surface of endothelial cells (, ). Instead of directly lysing endothelial cells, viral infection initiates a strong innate and adaptive immune response, along with an inflammatory cascade. This results in endothelial barrier dysfunction, which can be clinically observed as increased vascular permeability, thrombocytopenia, coagulation disturbances, and acute kidney injury (AKI) (, ). Clinically, HFRS classically manifests five sequential phases: the febrile phase, hypotensive shock phase, oliguric phase, diuretic phase, and convalescent phase. Not all patients experience every phase in complete sequence; phase overlap frequently occurs, in which features of two or more phases appear simultaneously (). HFRS can be classified into four grades: mild, moderate, severe, and critical. In clinical practice, mild and moderate cases are often grouped together as a broad “mild” category, while severe and critical cases are grouped as “severe” (, –). However, the criteria for severe disease are not fully consistent across different hantavirus infections. For HTNV infection, severe HFRS is defined by a body temperature >40 °C, neurological symptoms, shock, oliguria lasting ≥5 days or anuria lasting ≥2 days, or hemorrhage in vital organs (, ). For PUUV-induced nephropathia epidemica (NE), severe cases are often characterized by severe AKI or shock (, ). Despite these differences, the definitions all highlight the essential features of severe HFRS, including hypotension or shock, severe AKI, a significant bleeding tendency, and multiple organ dysfunction (). Currently, no specific antiviral therapy is available, and the management of severe HFRS relies mainly on continuous renal replacement therapy (CRRT), mechanical ventilation, and vasopressor support (, , ). However, because of rapid progression to severe disease and the limited therapeutic window, intervention is often delayed, resulting in high mortality rates (). Therefore, early recognition of patients at risk of severe progression and prompt initiation of intensive care are critical for improving outcomes. In recent years, research on early warning of severe HFRS has advanced considerably across multiple levels, encompassing bedside signs, routine laboratory parameters, immunological markers, and emerging novel biomarkers. In this review, we comprehensively synthesize progress in the aforementioned areas and evaluate the predictive performance and translational potential of various biomarkers. We also discuss current challenges and future perspectives, with the aim of establishing an evidence base for early identification and precise management of severe HFRS. 2 Clinically accessible warning systems for early risk stratification Clinically accessible warning systems including bedside signs and routine laboratory parameters are the most important indicators for predicting severe HFRS. This section reviews the available evidence on bedside signs and standard laboratory tests for predicting severe HFRS. The goal is to provide a practical framework for early risk assessment. 2.1 Bedside signs of severe HFRS prediction Bedside signs offer unique discriminative value for early risk stratification in HFRS, particularly in the absence of laboratory data. The 2021 Chinese Expert Consensus on Prevention and Treatment of HFRS identifies several key warning indicators for severe cases. These include a history of travel to endemic areas or contact with rodents and their excreta within two months prior to onset, high fever (temperature >40 °C or febrile duration exceeding one week), severe gastrointestinal symptoms such as intense nausea and vomiting, psychiatric disturbances including agitation or delirium, marked conjunctival edema, and obvious bleeding tendency (). Regarding imaging findings, a retrospective analysis by Huang et al. of 191 patients with HFRS in southwestern China demonstrated that pleural effusion was an independent risk factor for progression to severe HFRS. Patients with pleural effusion had a 4.49-fold higher risk of severe progression compared to those without it, suggesting that this sign may reflect more extensive capillary leakage and systemic inflammation (). The quick Sequential Organ Failure Assessment (qSOFA) score also has shown significant value in predicting severe HFRS. Ma and colleagues conducted a multicenter study of 551 HFRS patients in Hubei Province. They demonstrated that an admission qSOFA score of 2 or higher was an independent risk factor for 30-day mortality. The qSOFA score is defined as meeting any two of the following criteria: respiratory rate ≥22 breaths/min, systolic blood pressure ≤100 mmHg, or altered mental status. This finding suggests that the qSOFA score, without reliance on any laboratory tests, can serve as a rapid triage tool for early identification of high-risk HFRS patients and for determining the need for intensive care unit admission (). Notably, the early warning indicators for severe HFRS vary across different age groups. Researchers at Tangdu Hospital have conducted stratified warning analyses for both older adults and children (, ). In the older-adult cohort (≥ 60 years), Li et al. reviewed 146 cases and identified several early warning signs using multivariate logistic regression. These included chest tightness or dyspnea, nausea or vomiting, decreased urine output (UO), skin and mucosal hemorrhage, and phase overlap (disease course spanning two or more typical phases). These findings suggest that assessment of older adults with HFRS should focus more on cardiopulmonary function, gastrointestinal symptoms, renal perfusion, coagulation status, and disease progression patterns (). In the pediatric cohort (<16 years), the same group analyzed 103 cases. They found that conjunctival edema, hypotensive shock, and elevated serum creatinine (Cr) were key early warning indicators. This suggests that assessment in children should focus more on fluid extravasation, circulatory status, and early renal changes. Taken together, risk assessment should combine exposure history, consensus-based warning signs, bedside scores, and age-specific findings (). 2.2 Routine laboratory parameters for early warning of severe HFRS 2.2.1 Blood cell indices and inflammatory markers Blood count and routine inflammatory markers are the most accessible laboratory indicators for evaluating the systemic host response in HFRS. Markedly elevated white blood cell count (WBC) and severely reduced platelet count (PLT) have long been recognized as warning signs for HFRS severity (, ). The 2021 Expert Consensus has established WBC >30 × 109/L and PLT <20 × 109/L as definitive severity warning thresholds (). This pattern has been consistently confirmed by multiple retrospective cohort studies from various regions. Yang et al. analyzed 109 HFRS cases in central China and found that the median WBC in the severe group (25.2 × 109/L) was significantly higher than in the mild group (12.6 × 109/L), while the median PLT (22 × 109/L) was significantly lower than in the mild group (54 × 109/L) (). Chen et al. further examined the association between these two indicators and adverse outcomes in a cohort of 395 HFRS patients in northwestern China. The results showed that the median WBC in the non-survivor group (23.19 × 109/L) was significantly higher than in the survivor group (13.29 × 109/L), while the median PLT (22 × 109/L) was significantly lower than in the survivor group (41 × 109/L) (). Platelet distribution width (PDW) may provide information on platelet activation and function beyond that conveyed by PLT alone. Fan et al. studied 260 HFRS patients and found that PDW on the first day of admission increased significantly with disease severity. Of note, in critically ill patients, the association between PDW and prognosis was reversed, with non-survivors exhibiting lower PDW than survivors. This reversal may reflect exhausted marrow hematopoietic compensation, where declining PDW portends worse outcomes (). The neutrophil-to-red blood cell ratio (NRR) and neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR), as simple readouts of systemic inflammation, have demonstrated predictive value across multiple viral species. Xiao et al. analyzed 342 HTNV-HFRS cases in Xi’an and found that NRR was significantly elevated in the severe/critical group, with optimal discriminative performance for severity grading, whereas NLR was significantly elevated in the non-survivor group, with optimal performance for 28-day all-cause mortality prediction. Both markers are accessible at the bedside, with NRR more suitable for early severity stratification and NLR better aligned with mortality risk assessment (). In PUUV infection, Nusshag et al. analyzed 32 PUUV-infected patients in Germany and showed that peak NLR was significantly elevated in severe patients with hospitalization exceeding five days, suggesting that systemic neutrophil-lymphocyte imbalance is an important accompanying feature of PUUV severity (). Procalcitonin (PCT), as an indicator reflecting the severity of infection and inflammation, has shown predictive value across multiple independent studies. Duan et al. found that serum PCT level at emergency department admission was an independent risk factor for severe progression in HFRS patients, with the median PCT in the severe group significantly higher than in the mild group (8.12 vs. 1.39 ng/mL); an admission PCT exceeding 2.97 ng/mL demonstrated good predictive value for severity, with an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.862, and a sensitivity of 88.0% (). Chen et al. found in 272 HFRS patients that admission PCT levels increased significantly with disease severity, with an AUC of 0.792 for predicting 28-day survival/death at an optimal cutoff of 2.28 ng/mL, outperforming WBC (AUC 0.769) (). Che et al. further confirmed in a retrospective study of 373 HFRS patients that the median admission PCT in the severe group was significantly higher than in the mild group (3.8 vs. 1.3 ng/mL), with an AUC of 0.824 for predicting severity; PCT was also significantly higher in non-survivors than in survivors (3.6 vs. 1.7 ng/mL), with an AUC of 0.737 for predicting hospital mortality (). Huang et al. confirmed in a retrospective cohort of 191 HFRS patients in southwestern China that PCT was an independent risk factor for severe progression, with each 1 ng/mL increase in PCT associated with approximately 33% higher odds of developing severe disease (). Yu et al. also confirmed in a cohort of 384 HFRS patients that PCT was significantly higher in the severe/critical group than in the mild/moderate group, with multivariate logistic regression confirming elevated PCT as an independent predictor of severe progression (). These results indicate that PCT is a useful marker for assessing both disease severity and short-term mortality in HFRS, and may help identify high-risk patients early. Unlike PCT, C-reactive protein (CRP) showed limited independent value for HFRS severity prediction. Che et al. studied 373 HFRS patients and found that admission CRP was significantly higher in the severe group than in the mild group (median 42.1 vs. 29.5 mg/L). However, its AUC for severity prediction was only 0.614, far below that of PCT (0.824) (). Yang et al. also found that although the median CRP was significantly higher in the severe group than in the mild group (51.0 vs. 30.9 mg/L), CRP was deemed to lack independent incremental value during least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression variable selection and was therefore not included in the final prediction model (). Chen et al. further confirmed in 272 HFRS patients that admission CRP was elevated across all severity grades (mean approximately 30.1 to 33.96 mg/L for each group), with no statistically significant difference among the four groups, indicating that CRP does not exhibit a gradient change with disease severity. However, CRP retains potential utility in assessing secondary bacterial infection: the median CRP in the infected group was significantly higher than in the non-infected group (43.2 vs. 26.4 mg/L, p < 0.001), with an AUC of 0.588 for predicting secondary bacterial infection (p = 0.005). Although this represents moderate-to-weak performance, it is statistically significant, whereas PCT showed no discriminative capacity in this setting (). Therefore, CRP is more suitable as an auxiliary marker for bacterial infection rather than an independent predictor of HFRS severity. The predictive role of serum albumin (ALB) and hemoglobin (Hb) remains controversial. The 2021 Expert Consensus lists serum ALB below 15 g/L as a severity warning indicator (). Huang et al. reported that the median admission ALB was significantly lower in the severe group than in the mild group (25.45 vs. 29.80 g/L) on univariate analysis. After LASSO screening, multivariate logistic regression confirmed ALB as an independent protective factor against severe progression. Each 1 g/L increase in ALB was associated with an approximate 14% reduction in HFRS severity risk (). However, both Duan et al. and Yang et al. demonstrated that although ALB was lower in the severe group at the univariate level, it was not an independent risk factor in multivariate models, suggesting that its predictive power might be affected by other coexisting indicators (, ). Hb findings are also inconsistent. Huang et al. found no significant difference in admission Hb between severe and mild groups (), whereas Yang et al. reported significantly lower Hb in severe cases, though this association did not persist in multivariate analysis (). These findings indicate that the independent value of ALB and Hb as severity warning indicators is not yet stable and should be interpreted in conjunction with other indicators. 2.2.2 Coagulation function assessment Coagulation and fibrinolysis system disorders represent core processes in HFRS severity progression and are major causes of severe hemorrhage and death. Multiple studies have confirmed that severe HFRS patients present with typical coagulation activation and consumption at admission. In a cohort of 395 patients with HTNV-HFRS, Chen et al. found that non-survivors exhibited significantly prolonged prothrombin time (PT) and activated partial thromboplastin time (APTT), sharply decreased fibrinogen (Fib), and markedly elevated D-dimer and fibrinogen degradation products (FDP) at admission. The study also found that the abnormal detection rates of D-dimer and FDP were significantly higher than those of PT, APTT, and Fib, suggesting that early hyperfibrinolysis dominates the coagulation disorders in HFRS and should be a priority in routine assessment (). Disseminated intravascular coagulation (DIC) represents the end-stage of coagulation failure. Sundberg et al. applied the International Society on Thrombosis and Hemostasis (ISTH) criteria to perform DIC scoring in 106 patients with HFRS and found that approximately 18.9% to 28.3% of the patients met the diagnostic criteria for overt DIC. DIC status was significantly associated with moderate to severe disease and bleeding. Notably, a modified ISTH scoring template incorporating the fibrinogen-to-CRP ratio to adjust for inflammatory influence demonstrated superior predictive performance. These findings suggest that DIC scoring could serve as an effective risk stratification tool in HFRS (). Thrombomodulin (TM) has been recogn…

papers.title: SARS, H1N1, EBOLA, COVID-19, MPOX, H5N1 AND HANTAVIRUS: IS HUMANITY ENTERING A NEW ERA OF PANDEMIC? IS TÜRKİYE PREPARED FOR THE NEXT GLOBAL OUTBREAK?
papers.abstract: The emergence and re-emergence of infectious diseases pose persistent challenges to global health security. Outbreaks such as severe acute respiratory syndrome (SARS), influenza A(H1N1), Ebola virus disease, coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19), mpox, avian influenza A(H5N1), and hantavirus infections highlight the need for effective preparedness against emerging infectious threats. The concept of “Disease X” further emphasizes the importance of preparing for unknown pathogens that may cause future epidemics or pandemics. This study aimed to examine major infectious disease outbreaks and assess Türkiye’s preparedness for potential future global outbreaks. A descriptive review design was employed, based on a structured literature search and document analysis of scientific publications and institutional reports. The findings were organized and interpreted using a SWOT framework. The analysis identified healthcare infrastructure, intensive care capacity, digital health systems, and experience gained during the COVID-19 pandemic as potential strengths. However, challenges related to healthcare workforce capacity, zoonotic disease surveillance, public health literacy, coordination across human, animal, and environmental health sectors, and dependence on external sources for certain biotechnological products may constrain preparedness. Climate change, environmental disruption, international travel, migration, and global trade were identified as factors that may influence the emergence and spread of infectious diseases. Strengthening integrated surveillance and early warning systems, improving intersectoral coordination through the One Health approach, enhancing domestic vaccine and diagnostic production capacity, and expanding community-based public health education may help improve Türkiye’s preparedness for future outbreaks. These findings highlight the importance of sustained, multisectoral preparedness for emerging infectious disease threats.

Outbreaks such as severe acute respiratory syndrome (SARS), influenza A(H1N1), Ebola virus disease, coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19), mpox, avian influenza A(H5N1), and hantavirus infections highlight the need for effective preparedness against emerging infectious threats. The concept of “Disease X” further emphasizes the importance of preparing for unknown pathogens that may cause future epidemics or pandemics. This study aimed to examine major infectious disease outbreaks and assess Türkiye’s preparedness for potential future global outbreaks. A descriptive review design was employed, based on a structured literature search and document analysis of scientific publications and institutional reports. The findings were organized and interpreted using a SWOT framework. The analysis identified healthcare infrastructure, intensive care capacity, digital health systems, and experience gained during the COVID-19 pandemic as potential strengths. However, challenges related to healthcare workforce capacity, zoonotic disease surveillance, public health literacy, coordination across human, animal, and environmental health sectors, and dependence on external sources for certain biotechnological products may constrain preparedness. Climate change, environmental disruption, international travel, migration, and global trade were identified as factors that may influence the emergence and spread of infectious diseases. Strengthening integrated surveillance and early warning systems, improving intersectoral coordination through the One Health approach, enhancing domestic vaccine and diagnostic production capacity, and expanding community-based public health education may help improve Türkiye’s preparedness for future outbreaks. These findings highlight the importance of sustained, multisectoral preparedness for emerging infectious disease threats.

papers.title: ArHa: A globally standardised, relational database of arenavirus and hantavirus sampling in wild small mammal populations
papers.abstract: Arenaviruses and hantaviruses are globally distributed zoonotic pathogens primarily hosted by small mammals. Efforts to map their ecological drivers and predict spillover risk are hindered by the fragmentation of historical surveillance data across the primary literature, compounded by shifting host nomenclature and variable geographic precision. We present ArHa, a database of 123,101 host occurrence and pathogen diagnostic records derived from a systematic review of published wild small mammal sampling. The dataset standardises host and pathogen taxonomies, resolves records of the same animals published in more than one paper, and classifies the spatial resolution and reliability of each coordinate to support bias-aware spatial epidemiology. To accurately preserve complex study designs, such as multiple diagnostic assays or genetic sequences derived from a single host, ArHa is structured as a four-tier relational database. This architecture handles many-to-one relationships and supports linkage without data duplication. The dataset is distributed as compressed Apache Parquet files for programmatic analysis and as a Darwin Core Archive, so that it can be read by standard biodiversity data tools. An accompanying interactive web application, the ArHa Database Explorer, allows users to filter, visualise, and export subsets of the database without requiring programming expertise. All data, extraction scripts, and the interactive web application are openly accessible via a permanent Zenodo repository.

papers.title: Hantavirus on a Cruise Ship: What COVID-19 Taught Us.
papers.abstract: Delayed recognition of the mechanics of aerosol transmission-the primary mode of spread of severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2)-at the beginning of the coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) pandemic led to inadequate early recommendations regarding nonpharmaceutical interventions and poor initial messaging about how to reduce infection risk. We highlight key epidemiological details of Andes virus (ANDV) transmission on the MV Hondius cruise ship and during prior reported outbreaks with confirmed person-to-person spread in Argentina, which, together, suggest aerosol spread may be a key mechanism of transmission of ANDV between source cases and susceptible contacts in permissible environmental settings.
papers.journal: Clinical infectious diseases : an official publication of the Infectious Diseases Society of America

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to address the knowledge gap regarding the transmission dynamics of hantaviruses, particularly highlighting the lessons learned from the SARS-CoV-2 pandemic about aerosol transmission mechanisms and their implications for public health preparedness.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study analyzed epidemiological details of Andes virus (ANDV) transmission on the MV Hondius cruise ship and during prior reported outbreaks in Argentina, focusing on person-to-person spread patterns in permissible environmental settings.
analysis.methods: The authors reviewed epidemiological data and transmission patterns of ANDV from the MV Hondius cruise ship and prior outbreaks, emphasizing the environmental and behavioral factors that facilitated aerosol spread.
analysis.main_results: The analysis of ANDV transmission on the MV Hondius cruise ship and prior outbreaks suggests that aerosol spread may be a key mechanism of transmission between source cases and susceptible contacts in permissible environmental settings.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret that the transmission patterns observed for ANDV provide novel insights into the potential role of aerosol spread in hantavirus transmission, drawing parallels with the SARS-CoV-2 pandemic.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings can inform improved surveillance and prevention strategies for hantaviruses, particularly in enclosed environments where aerosol transmission may occur.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its reliance on reported outbreaks and lacks direct experimental evidence, resulting in moderate confidence in the interpretation of aerosol transmission as a key mechanism.

The authors suggest that these findings can inform improved public health strategies for hantavirus surveillance and prevention. However, the study is limited by its reliance on observational data and lacks direct experimental evidence, resulting in moderate confidence in its conclusions.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在解决有关 传播 动态的知识差距,特别强调从 SARS-CoV-2 大流行中吸取的有关气溶胶 传播 机制的经验教训及其对公共卫生准备的影响。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究分析了 MV Hondius 游轮上以及之前报道的阿根廷 暴发 期间安第斯病毒 (ANDV) 传播 的流行病学详细信息,重点关注在允许的环境条件下人与人之间的传播模式。
elements_zh.methods: 作者回顾了 MV Hondius 游轮和之前的 暴发 的 ANDV 流行病学数据和 传播 模式,强调了促进气溶胶传播的环境和行为因素。
elements_zh.main_results: 对 MV Hondius 游轮上的 ANDV 传播 和之前的 暴发 的分析表明,气溶胶传播可能是在允许的环境条件下源病例和易感接触者之间 传播 的关键机制。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者解释说,观察到的 ANDV 传播 模式为汉坦病毒传播 中气溶胶传播的潜在作用提供了新的见解,与 SARS-CoV-2 大流行相似。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现可以为改进 监测 和汉坦病毒的预防策略提供信息,特别是在可能出现气溶胶 传播 的封闭环境中。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究受限于其对报道的 暴发 的依赖,并且缺乏直接的实验证据,导致对气溶胶 传播 作为关键机制的解释的信心中等。

papers.title: Case Report: Hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome caused by Seoul orthohantavirus mimicking severe acute pancreatitis: dynamic imaging evolution and pathogen confirmation by mNGS
papers.abstract: Background Hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS) is a zoonotic disease caused by orthohantaviruses, characterized by fever, thrombocytopenia, renal impairment, and capillary leak syndrome. Its atypical presentations can closely mimic acute pancreatitis (AP), posing substantial diagnostic challenges. Case presentation A 33-year-old man presented with fever, vomiting, and watery diarrhea. Initial computed tomography (CT) revealed peripancreatic and perirenal exudation suggestive of severe acute pancreatitis. He already had profound thrombocytopenia on admission (nadir 29 × 109/L), progressive renal impairment, hematuria, and proteinuria, without typical pancreatitis risk factors or elevated pancreatic enzymes. Contrast-enhanced CT demonstrated progressive retroperitoneal exudation with relatively mild pancreatic parenchymal changes and newly developed bilateral pleural effusion. Whole-blood metagenomic next-generation sequencing (mNGS) detected high-copy Seoul orthohantavirus, with concurrent hepatitis B virus. The patient recovered fully with supportive care, intravenous immunoglobulin, and symptomatic treatment; pre-discharge ultrasound showed normal pancreatic morphology. Conclusion Seoul orthohantavirus infection can closely mimic severe acute pancreatitis clinically and radiologically. Disproportionate thrombocytopenia, renal involvement, and progressive retroperitoneal exudation with preserved pancreatic parenchyma are key diagnostic clues, and mNGS enables early definitive pathogen confirmation, facilitating appropriate management.

The patient recovered fully with supportive care, intravenous immunoglobulin, and symptomatic treatment. The study highlights the importance of considering hantavirus infections in patients with atypical pancreatitis presentations and underscores the utility of mNGS for early pathogen confirmation. The findings suggest that disproportionate thrombocytopenia, renal involvement, and progressive retroperitoneal exudation with preserved pancreatic parenchyma are key diagnostic clues. However, the study's single-case design limits generalizability, and the evidence is strong for the specific diagnosis of Seoul orthohantavirus infection.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 肾综合征出血热 (HFRS) 是一种由正汉坦病毒引起的人畜共患疾病,其特征为发烧、血小板减少、肾功能损害和毛细血管渗漏综合征。其非典型表现与急性胰腺炎(AP)非常相似,给诊断带来了巨大的挑战。

elements_zh.methods: 采用全血宏基因组下一代测序(mNGS)检测病原体,并采用动态成像监测患者病情。
elements_zh.main_results: 最初的计算机断层扫描 (CT) 显示胰周和肾周渗出,提示严重急性胰腺炎。增强CT显示进行性腹膜后渗出,伴有相对轻微的胰腺实质改变和新出现的双侧胸腔积液。通过支持治疗、静脉注射免疫球蛋白和有症状的 治疗,患者完全康复;出院前超声显示胰腺形态正常。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者解释说,首尔正汉坦病毒感染在临床和放射学上与重症急性胰腺炎非常相似。该病例强调了将汉坦病毒作为非典型胰腺炎患者的鉴别诊断 诊断 的重要性。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,需要提高对出现类似重症急性胰腺炎症状的患者的汉坦病毒感染的认识,特别是在汉坦病毒流行的地区。使用 mNGS 进行早期病原体确认有助于及时、适当的管理。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究是单一的病例报告,限制了普遍性。然而,使用mNGS进行病原体确认为首尔正汉坦病毒感染的诊断提供了强有力的证据,详细的影像学结果支持重症急性胰腺炎的临床和放射学模拟。

papers.title: Hantavirus: An Emerging Global Zoonotic Threat—From Molecular Basis to Clinical Management and Public Health Perspectives
papers.abstract: Hantavirus infection is an emerging zoonotic viral disease caused by hantaviruses of the family Hantaviridae, primarily transmitted to humans through exposure to infected rodent urine, feces, saliva, or contaminated aerosols. The disease presents mainly in two clinical forms: Hemorrhagic Fever with Renal Syndrome (HFRS), prevalent in Asia and Europe, and Hantavirus Pulmonary Syndrome (HPS)/Hantavirus Cardiopulmonary Syndrome (HCPS), predominantly reported in the Americas. The historical recognition of hantavirus began during the Korean War (1950–1953), when thousands of soldiers developed Korean hemorrhagic fever. In 1978, Ho-Wang Lee isolated the Hantaan virus from Apodemus agrarius, marking a major scientific breakthrough. Subsequent decades witnessed the identification of multiple hantavirus species, including Seoul, Puumala, Dobrava-Belgrade, Sin Nombre, and Andes viruses, each associated with distinct rodent reservoirs and clinical manifestations. A major epidemiological milestone occurred in 1993 with the outbreak of Hantavirus Pulmonary Syndrome in the Four Corners region of the United States, leading to the discovery of Sin Nombre virus. Increasing urbanization, climate change, deforestation, and closer human–rodent interactions have contributed to the global emergence of hantavirus infections in the 21st century. Advances in molecular diagnostics, including reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR) and serological testing, have enhanced disease surveillance and early diagnosis. This review highlights the historical evolution, epidemiology, transmission, and growing public health significance of hantavirus infection worldwide. Keywords: Hantavirus infection; Hemorrhagic Fever with Renal Syndrome (HFRS); Hantavirus Pulmonary

papers.title: A Case Report of Hantavirus Capillary Leak Syndrome in the Southwestern United States.
papers.abstract: Hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome (HCPS) is a rare but frequently fatal viral disease endemic to the Americas, transmitted primarily through inhalation of aerosolized rodent excreta. Early symptoms are nonspecific, but the disease can rapidly progress to severe respiratory compromise and shock due to profound capillary leak. We report the case of a previously healthy 20-year-old man who initially presented with abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, and progressive weakness after occupational exposure on a ranch in southwestern Arizona. He quickly developed hemoconcentration (hematocrit 58%), thrombocytopenia (17,000 cells/μL), septic shock, and noncardiogenic pulmonary edema. The initial infectious workup was negative. His clinical course was complicated by respiratory failure requiring intubation and vasopressor support. Computed tomography of his chest showed pulmonary edema and large bilateral pleural effusions despite aggressive diuresis, requiring bilateral chest tubes. He gradually improved with supportive care, was successfully extubated, weaned off oxygen, and discharged home with outpatient rehabilitation. His diagnosis was later confirmed with a serum ELISA test which was positive for hantavirus IgM and IgG. This case highlights the diagnostic complexity of HCPS, particularly when gastrointestinal symptoms predominate early in the illness. In endemic areas with rodent exposure history, hemoconcentration and thrombocytopenia, along with signs of volume overload and rapidly progressive acute respiratory failure, should raise suspicion for hantavirus infection. Identification and supportive care are the mainstay of treatment. Although this patient did not require ECMO, transfer to an ECMO center may be beneficial to support recovery during the cardiopulmonary phase, as recommended by the Centers for Disease Control.

papers.title_zh: 美国西南部的 病例报告 毛细血管渗漏综合征。
papers.source_body_en: Hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome (HCPS) is a rare but frequently fatal viral disease endemic to the Americas, transmitted primarily through inhalation of aerosolized rodent excreta. Early symptoms are nonspecific, but the disease can rapidly progress to severe respiratory compromise and shock due to profound capillary leak. We report the case of a previously healthy 20-year-old man who initially presented with abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, and progressive weakness after occupational exposure on a ranch in southwestern Arizona. He quickly developed hemoconcentration (hematocrit 58%), thrombocytopenia (17,000 cells/μL), septic shock, and noncardiogenic pulmonary edema. The initial infectious workup was negative. His clinical course was complicated by respiratory failure requiring intubation and vasopressor support. Computed tomography of his chest showed pulmonary edema and large bilateral pleural effusions despite aggressive diuresis, requiring bilateral chest tubes. He gradually improved with supportive care, was successfully extubated, weaned off oxygen, and discharged home with outpatient rehabilitation. His diagnosis was later confirmed with a serum ELISA test which was positive for hantavirus IgM and IgG. This case highlights the diagnostic complexity of HCPS, particularly when gastrointestinal symptoms predominate early in the illness. In endemic areas with rodent exposure history, hemoconcentration and thrombocytopenia, along with signs of volume overload and rapidly progressive acute respiratory failure, should raise suspicion for hantavirus infection. Identification and supportive care are the mainstay of treatment. Although this patient did not require ECMO, transfer to an ECMO center may be beneficial to support recovery during the cardiopulmonary phase, as recommended by the Centers for Disease Control.

papers.title: Predictive Surveillance for Andes Virus Transmission in the Americas
papers.abstract: The 2026 Andes virus outbreak linked to the M/V Hondius cruise ship exposed limitations in conventional, case-based surveillance for zoonotic threats with potential person-to-person transmission. In the present opinion and analysis article, the authors argue that predictive surveillance, supported by artificial intelligence, ecological modeling, and the One Health approach, can strengthen preparedness for hantavirus transmission in the Americas. Current evidence suggests that selected models that incorporate epidemiological, climatic, environmental, and rodent-related variables may provide an anticipatory window of 2 to 12 months, depending on context and data inputs. However, implementation requires more than technical capacity. It depends on interoperable multisectoral data, transparent model governance, local validation, sustainable financing, and technology transfer to avoid widening inequities between health systems. Predictive surveillance should complement conventional surveillance by supporting risk communication, rodent monitoring, laboratory preparedness, and targeted public health action in areas where ecological and epidemiological signals converge.

papers.title_zh: 美洲安第斯山脉病毒 传播 的预测 监测
papers.source_body_en: The 2026 Andes virus outbreak linked to the M/V Hondius cruise ship exposed limitations in conventional, case-based surveillance for zoonotic threats with potential person-to-person transmission. In the present opinion and analysis article, the authors argue that predictive surveillance, supported by artificial intelligence, ecological modeling, and the One Health approach, can strengthen preparedness for hantavirus transmission in the Americas. Current evidence suggests that selected models that incorporate epidemiological, climatic, environmental, and rodent-related variables may provide an anticipatory window of 2 to 12 months, depending on context and data inputs. However, implementation requires more than technical capacity. It depends on interoperable multisectoral data, transparent model governance, local validation, sustainable financing, and technology transfer to avoid widening inequities between health systems. Predictive surveillance should complement conventional surveillance by supporting risk communication, rodent monitoring, laboratory preparedness, and targeted public health action in areas where ecological and epidemiological signals converge.

papers.title: The 2026 Andes hantavirus outbreak: a renewed call for global zoonotic preparedness
papers.abstract: The 2026 cluster of Andes virus (ANDV) infection linked to the expedition cruise ship MV Hondius resulted in 13 cases (12 laboratory-confirmed and one probable), including three deaths, and required the monitoring of more than 650 contacts across more than 30 countries and territories before the World Health Organization (WHO) declared the outbreak over on 2 July 2026. Available evidence suggests a single land-based zoonotic exposure before embarkation, followed by limited person-to-person transmission on board. Although WHO assessed the global risk as low throughout, the event exposed recurring weaknesses in zoonotic preparedness, including delayed clinical recognition in a remote setting, maritime outbreak protocols oriented toward other pathogens, and the burden of multinational contact tracing for an infection with an incubation period of up to 6 weeks. This editorial examines these lessons in light of earlier ANDV outbreaks and argues for closer integration of One Health surveillance, maritime health security, and the International Health Regulations in preparing for rare but high-consequence zoonoses.
papers.journal: International Journal of Surgery: Global Health

papers.abstract_zh: 与远征游轮 MV Hondius 相关的 2026 年安第斯病毒 (ANDV) 群感染导致 13 例病例(12 例实验室确诊病例,1 例疑似病例),其中包括 3 例死亡,在世界卫生组织 (WHO) 于 2026 年 7 月 2 日宣布 暴发 结束之前,需要对 30 多个国家和地区的 650 多名接触者进行监测。现有证据表明,在登船,然后船上进行有限的人际 传播。尽管世卫组织自始至终评估全球风险较低,但该事件暴露了人畜共患病防备工作中反复出现的弱点,包括偏远地区的临床识别延迟、针对其他病原体的海上 暴发 方案,以及潜伏期长达 6 周的感染的多国接触者追踪负担。这篇社论根据早期的 ANDV 暴发 回顾了这些教训,并主张将 One Health 监测、海上卫生安全和国际卫生条例更紧密地结合起来,为罕见但后果严重的人畜共患病做好准备。

analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究分析了 MV Hondius 号远征游轮上的 2026 暴发安第斯病毒(ANDV),该病毒导致 13 例病例(12 例实验室确诊病例和 1 例疑似病例)和 3 例死亡,并在 30 多个国家和地区监测了 650 多名接触者。
analysis_zh.methods: 该研究回顾了暴发的流行病学和临床特征,包括接触者监测和世界卫生组织(WHO)对全球风险的评估。
analysis_zh.main_results: 暴发 与登船前的一次陆上人畜共患病接触有关,船上人与人之间的 传播 有限,世界卫生组织于 2026 年 7 月 2 日宣布 暴发 结束。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将这些发现解释为暴露了人畜共患病防范方面反复出现的弱点,特别是在偏远地区和海上卫生协议方面,并主张将 One Health 监测 与国际卫生法规更紧密地结合起来。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果强调了通过改进 监测、海上卫生安全和国际合作加强全球人畜共患病防范的重要性,特别是针对 ANDV 等罕见但后果严重的病原体。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究基于现有证据和世卫组织的评估,在捕捉 暴发 动态的全部范围方面可能存在局限性,但由于其依赖于报告的结果和影响,证据的强度被认为是中等的。

papers.title: Age-stratified associations between meteorological factors and haemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome in Shaanxi Province, China, 2005–2020: a distributed lag non-linear analysis aligned with vaccination programme eligibility ages
papers.abstract: Abstract Background Shaanxi Province reports the highest burden of haemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS) in China, concentrated in the Guanzhong Plain. Whether meteorological sensitivity differs across age strata aligned with the eligibility ages of the national vaccination programme (16–60 years) has not been quantified. Methods We obtained monthly HFRS case counts for 27 age groups in Shaanxi, 2005–2020 (26,677 cases), constructed incidence with census-interpolated denominators, and aggregated cases into vaccination-aligned strata: 0–19, 20–59 and ≥ 60 years. Exposures came from 12 China Meteorological Administration surface stations. Quasi-Poisson distributed lag non-linear models were fitted per stratum for monthly mean temperature, relative humidity and precipitation (lag 0–6 months); long-term trends (2004–2024) were assessed by joinpoint regression. Results No statistically significant joinpoints were identified; incidence declined gradually and non-significantly (annual percent change − 0.83%/year, 95% confidence interval [CI] − 4.68 to 3.07), with multi-year cycles and a 60% fall in 2024. Stratum-specific incidence was lowest at 0–19 years (1.77/100,000) and highest at ≥ 60 years (6.45/100,000). Low temperature was associated with elevated risk in all main models (cumulative relative risk [RR] at − 1.2°C: 2.15–3.39; intervals wide and overlapping), with no effect modification by stratum (interaction p = 0.999); cold-temperature estimates attenuated below unity under calendar-year-indicator control, indicating entanglement with epidemic cycles. Hydro-meteorological associations were positive but imprecise in the main models: at 80% relative humidity, cumulative RRs were 2.44 (95% CI 0.44–13.6), 1.92 (0.67–5.46) and 3.16 (0.97–10.2), and 150 mm precipitation gave 3.05 (1.06–8.82) in the 20–59 group, significant only on the original scale. Under the year-indicator specification these estimates strengthened severalfold (humidity 8.70, 3.11, 4.36; precipitation 6.56); the 0–19 and ≥ 60 year humidity associations and the precipitation association survived false-discovery-rate control and are hypothesis-generating. Colder autumns preceded heavier epidemic peaks (exploratory; Spearman ρ = −0.64, p = 0.010). Conclusions Meteorological conditions were associated with HFRS risk across vaccination-aligned age strata in Shaanxi. Humidity and precipitation showed positive but imprecise, specification-sensitive associations, whereas the low-temperature association could not be separated from multi-year epidemic cycles. Adults aged ≥ 60 years had the highest incidence and elevated hydro-meteorological sensitivity. On the basis of incidence burden, these findings support evaluation of extending HFRS vaccination beyond age 60.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to investigate whether meteorological factors have different associations with haemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS) across age groups aligned with the national vaccination programme eligibility ages (16–60 years).
analysis.study_design_and_population: A distributed lag non-linear analysis was conducted using monthly HFRS case counts from 27 age groups in Shaanxi Province, China, between 2005 and 2020, with 26,677 cases. Cases were aggregated into three vaccination-aligned age strata: 0–19, 20–59 and ≥ 60 years.
analysis.methods: Quasi-Poisson distributed lag non-linear models were fitted for each age stratum using monthly mean temperature, relative humidity and precipitation data from 12 meteorological stations, with lags ranging from 0 to 6 months. Long-term trends were assessed using joinpoint regression from 2004 to 2024.
analysis.main_results: No statistically significant joinpoints were identified, and incidence declined gradually and non-significantly (annual percent change − 0.83%/year, 95% confidence interval [CI] − 4.68 to 3.07). A 60% fall in incidence was observed in 2024. Low temperature was associated with elevated risk in all main models, with cumulative relative risks (RRs) ranging from 2.15 to 3.39 at −1.2°C, although these estimates overlapped widely. Under calendar-year-indicator control, cold-temperature estimates attenuated below unity, suggesting entanglement with epidemic cycles.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted that meteorological conditions are associated with HFRS risk across vaccination-aligned age strata, but the associations for humidity and precipitation were positive and imprecise, showing sensitivity to model specifications, while the low-temperature association could not be separated from multi-year epidemic cycles.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that meteorological factors may influence HFRS risk differently across age groups, which could inform targeted surveillance and prevention strategies, particularly for adults aged ≥ 60 years who had the highest incidence and elevated hydro-meteorological sensitivity.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study's evidence is limited by the inability to separate low-temperature associations from epidemic cycles, and the imprecision and specification sensitivity of humidity and precipitation associations. The confidence in the findings is moderate.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the age-stratified associations between meteorological factors and haemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS) in Shaanxi Province, China, from 2005 to 2020. It found that low temperature was consistently associated with increased HFRS risk across all age groups, but associations with humidity and precipitation were imprecise and sensitive to model specifications. The study suggests that meteorological conditions may influence HFRS risk differently across age strata aligned with vaccination eligibility, with adults aged ≥ 60 years showing the highest incidence and sensitivity. However, the findings are limited by the entanglement of temperature associations with epidemic cycles and the imprecision of other meteorological factors. The evidence is moderate in strength, highlighting the need for further research to clarify these relationships.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在调查气象因素是否与符合国家 疫苗接种 计划资格年龄(16-60 岁)的不同年龄组的肾综合征出血热 (HFRS) 存在不同的关联。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 利用 2005 年至 2020 年间中国陕西省 27 个年龄组的每月 HFRS 病例数(26,677 例)进行分布式滞后非线性分析。病例被汇总为三个与 疫苗接种 一致的年龄层:0-19 岁、20-59 岁和 ≥ 60 岁。
elements_zh.methods: 利用12个气象站月平均气温、相对湿度和降水数据,对各年龄层拟合拟泊松分布滞后非线性模型,滞后范围为0~6个月。使用 2004 年至 2024 年的连接点回归评估长期趋势。
elements_zh.main_results: 未发现具有统计显着性的连接点,发病率 逐渐且不显着地下降(年百分比变化 - 0.83%/年,95% 置信区间 [CI] - 4.68 至 3.07)。2024 年,发病率 下降了 60%。在所有主要模型中,低温都与风险升高相关,在 -1.2°C 时,累积相对风险 (RR) 范围为 2.15 至 3.39,尽管这些估计值广泛重叠。在日历年指标控制下,寒冷气温估计值减弱至统一以下,表明与流行病周期纠缠在一起。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者解释说,气象条件与 疫苗接种 年龄层的 HFRS 风险相关,但与湿度和降水的关联是正向且不精确的,显示出对模型规范的敏感性,而低温关联无法与多年流行周期分开。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,气象因素可能对不同年龄组的 HFRS 风险产生不同的影响,这可以为有针对性的 发病率 和预防策略提供信息,特别是对于年龄 ≥ 60 岁、发病率 最高和水文气象敏感性较高的成年人。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 由于无法将低温关联与流行病周期区分开来,以及湿度和降水关联的不精确性和规范敏感性,该研究的证据受到限制。研究结果的可信度为中等。

papers.abstract_zh: 摘要 背景 陕西省是中国肾综合征出血热(HFRS)负担最高的省份,集中在关中平原。与国家 疫苗接种 计划的资格年龄(16-60 岁)一致的年龄层之间的气象敏感性是否存在差异尚未得到量化。方法 我们获得了 2005 年至 2020 年陕西 27 个年龄组的每月 HFRS 病例数(26,677 例),用人口普查插值分母构建了 发病率,并将病例汇总到 疫苗接种 对齐的阶层:0-19、20-59 和 ≥ 60 岁。曝光来自12个中国气象局地面站。针对月平均温度、相对湿度和降水量,对每层拟合准泊松分布滞后非线性模型(滞后0-6个月);通过连接点回归评估长期趋势(2004-2024)。结果 未发现具有统计学意义的连接点;发病率 逐渐且不显着地下降(年度百分比变化 - 0.83%/年,95% 置信区间 [CI] - 4.68 至 3.07),具有多年周期,2024 年下降 60%。特定层 发病率 在 0-19 年最低(1.77/100,000),在 ≥ 时最高60 年(6.45/100,000)。在所有主要模型中,低温均与风险升高相关(−1.2°C 时的累积相对风险 [RR]:2.15–3.39;区间宽且重叠),且没有因阶层影响而产生的影响(交互作用 p = 0.999);在日历年指标控制下,寒冷气温估计值减弱至统一以下,表明与流行病周期纠缠在一起。水文气象关联是积极的,但在主要模型中并不精确:相对湿度为 80% 时,累积 RR 为 2.44 (95% CI 0.44–13.6)、1.92 (0.67–5.46) 和 3.16 (0.97–10.2),150 毫米降水量在模型中为 3.05 (1.06–8.82)。20-59 组,仅在原始量表上显着。根据年份指标规范,这些估计数增强了几倍(湿度 8.70、3.11、4.36;降水量 6.56);0-19年和≥60年的湿度关联和降水关联在错误发现率控制下幸存下来并正在生成假设。较冷的秋季先于较严重的流行高峰(探索性;Spearman ρ = -0.64,p = 0.010)。结论 陕西省 疫苗接种 年龄层的气象条件与 HFRS 风险相关。湿度和降水显示出积极但不精确的、规范敏感的关联,而低温关联无法与多年的流行周期分开。年龄≥ 60 岁的成年人具有最高的 发病率 和较高的水文气象敏感性。根据 发病率 负担,这些发现支持将 HFRS 发病率 延长至 60 岁以上的评估。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在调查气象因素是否与符合国家 疫苗接种 计划资格年龄(16-60 岁)的不同年龄组的肾综合征出血热 (HFRS) 存在不同的关联。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 利用 2005 年至 2020 年间中国陕西省 27 个年龄组的每月 HFRS 病例数(26,677 例)进行分布式滞后非线性分析。病例被汇总为三个与 疫苗接种 一致的年龄层:0-19 岁、20-59 岁和 ≥ 60 岁。
analysis_zh.methods: 利用12个气象站月平均气温、相对湿度和降水数据,对各年龄层拟合拟泊松分布滞后非线性模型,滞后范围为0~6个月。使用 2004 年至 2024 年的连接点回归评估长期趋势。
analysis_zh.main_results: 未发现具有统计显着性的连接点,发病率 逐渐且不显着地下降(年百分比变化 - 0.83%/年,95% 置信区间 [CI] - 4.68 至 3.07)。2024 年,发病率 下降了 60%。在所有主要模型中,低温都与风险升高相关,在 -1.2°C 时,累积相对风险 (RR) 范围为 2.15 至 3.39,尽管这些估计值广泛重叠。在日历年指标控制下,寒冷气温估计值减弱至统一以下,表明与流行病周期纠缠在一起。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者解释说,气象条件与 疫苗接种 年龄层的 HFRS 风险相关,但与湿度和降水的关联是正向且不精确的,显示出对模型规范的敏感性,而低温关联无法与多年流行周期分开。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,气象因素可能对不同年龄组的 HFRS 风险产生不同的影响,这可以为有针对性的 发病率 和预防策略提供信息,特别是对于年龄 ≥ 60 岁、发病率 最高和水文气象敏感性较高的成年人。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 由于无法将低温关联与流行病周期区分开来,以及湿度和降水关联的不精确性和规范敏感性,该研究的证据受到限制。研究结果的可信度为中等。

papers.title: Meteorological factors and haemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome incidence in ten provinces of China, 2005–2020: a two-stage, age- stratified distributed lag non-linear analysis
papers.abstract: Abstract Background Haemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS) is a rodent-borne zoonosis with its largest burden in China. Meteorological conditions influence transmission, but age- and endemic-type-specific associations remain unclear, and most multi-region studies lack population denominators. Methods We analysed 132,313 age-stratified HFRS cases reported during 2005–2020 in ten Chinese provinces, grouped by reservoir-host seasonality into Apodemus-type, Mixed-type and Rattus-type regions. Population denominators came from three censuses and revised intercensal series; monthly meteorological exposures came from quality-controlled national stations. Within each province and age stratum (0–19, 20–59, ≥ 60 years), we fitted quasi-Poisson distributed lag non-linear models (lag 0–6 months) with a log person-month offset and mutual exposure adjustment, pooling reduced curves by endemic type and stratum. Curve robustness was assessed using best linear unbiased predictions and a 2,000-draw bootstrap; null results were bounded by minimum detectable relative risks; provincial covariates were examined in meta-regressions. Results The 20–59-year stratum contributed 75.8% of cases (annual incidence 1.70 per 100,000, versus 0.33 at 0–19 and 1.57 at ≥ 60 years). In Apodemus-type provinces, precipitation showed an inverted-U association peaking at 175.9 mm (relative risk (RR) 2.73, 95% CI 1.44–5.18), strongest at ages 20–59 (190.6 mm, RR 3.08, 1.14–8.37) and robust to leave-one-province-out analysis (95th-percentile RR 1.44–3.52). Temperature peaked near 8.7°C (RR 1.44, 0.34–6.01). Humidity associations were weak on average but diverged across climate zones (dry-promoting in Shaanxi versus humid-promoting in Shandong), producing near-flat pooled curves (I2 up to 72.8%). The two Rattus-type provinces showed opposite temperature-curve directions (heat-promoting in subtropical Yunnan, cold-promoting in temperate Hebei) and are therefore reported per province. Age stratification eliminated Apodemus-type precipitation heterogeneity in the 0–19 and ≥ 60 strata (I2 = 0%). Provincial ageing rate explained temperature-curve heterogeneity (P = 0.004; I2 reduced from 60.0% to 40.2%). Detectability bounds indicated adequate power for moderate precipitation effects at working ages, but not for temperature extremes in sparse strata. Conclusions Meteorological–HFRS associations are structured by reservoir-host endemic type, concentrated in the working-age population, and modified by population ageing. Age-stratified designs with population denominators are essential for unbiased multi-region synthesis.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to investigate how meteorological factors influence the incidence of hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS) in different regions of China, as these associations are not well understood and most multi-region studies lack population denominators.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study analyzed 132,313 age-stratified HFRS cases reported in ten Chinese provinces between 2005 and 2020, grouped by reservoir-host seasonality into Apodemus-type, Mixed-type, and Rattus-type regions.
analysis.methods: Quasi-Poisson distributed lag non-linear models were fitted within each province and age stratum (0–19, 20–59, ≥ 60 years), with a log person-month offset and mutual exposure adjustment. Curve robustness was assessed using best linear unbiased predictions and a 2,000-draw bootstrap, while null results were bounded by minimum detectable relative risks.
analysis.main_results: The 20–59-year age stratum contributed 75.8% of cases, with an annual incidence of 1.70 per 100,000. In Apodemus-type provinces, precipitation showed an inverted-U association peaking at 175.9 mm (relative risk (RR) 2.73, 95% CI 1.44–5.18). Temperature peaked near 8.7°C (RR 1.44, 0.34–6.01). Humidity associations were weak but diverged across climate zones, producing near-flat pooled curves (I2 up to 72.8%). The two Rattus-type provinces showed opposite temperature-curve directions.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted that meteorological-HFRS associations are structured by reservoir-host endemic type, concentrated in the working-age population, and modified by population ageing.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings inform the need for age-stratified designs with population denominators to better understand and address the impact of meteorological factors on HFRS, particularly in working-age populations.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: Age stratification eliminated precipitation heterogeneity in the 0–19 and ≥ 60 strata, and provincial ageing rate explained temperature-curve heterogeneity. The evidence strength is moderate, as detectability bounds indicated adequate power for moderate precipitation effects but not for temperature extremes in sparse strata.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the association between meteorological factors and the incidence of hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS) in ten Chinese provinces from 2005 to 2020. It focused on how precipitation, temperature, and humidity influence HFRS, with particular attention to age-stratified populations and endemic types. The results showed that the 20–59-year age group had the highest incidence, with precipitation showing an inverted-U association and temperature peaking near 8.7°C. Humidity effects varied by climate zone, and Rattus-type provinces exhibited divergent temperature associations. The authors concluded that meteorological-HFRS relationships are shaped by reservoir-host endemic types and population ageing. The study's limitations include the elimination of precipitation heterogeneity in younger and older age groups and the reduced power for detecting temperature extremes in sparse strata. The findings highlight the importance of age-stratified designs for multi-region HFRS analysis.

analysis_en.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to investigate how meteorological factors influence the incidence of hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS) in different regions of China, as these associations are not well understood and most multi-region studies lack population denominators.
analysis_en.study_design_and_population: The study analyzed 132,313 age-stratified HFRS cases reported in ten Chinese provinces between 2005 and 2020, grouped by reservoir-host seasonality into Apodemus-type, Mixed-type, and Rattus-type regions.
analysis_en.methods: Quasi-Poisson distributed lag non-linear models were fitted within each province and age stratum (0–19, 20–59, ≥ 60 years), with a log person-month offset and mutual exposure adjustment. Curve robustness was assessed using best linear unbiased predictions and a 2,000-draw bootstrap, while null results were bounded by minimum detectable relative risks.
analysis_en.main_results: The 20–59-year age stratum contributed 75.8% of cases, with an annual incidence of 1.70 per 100,000. In Apodemus-type provinces, precipitation showed an inverted-U association peaking at 175.9 mm (relative risk (RR) 2.73, 95% CI 1.44–5.18). Temperature peaked near 8.7°C (RR 1.44, 0.34–6.01). Humidity associations were weak but diverged across climate zones, producing near-flat pooled curves (I2 up to 72.8%). The two Rattus-type provinces showed opposite temperature-curve directions.
analysis_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted that meteorological-HFRS associations are structured by reservoir-host endemic type, concentrated in the working-age population, and modified by population ageing.
analysis_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings inform the need for age-stratified designs with population denominators to better understand and address the impact of meteorological factors on HFRS, particularly in working-age populations.
analysis_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: Age stratification eliminated precipitation heterogeneity in the 0–19 and ≥ 60 strata, and provincial ageing rate explained temperature-curve heterogeneity. The evidence strength is moderate, as detectability bounds indicated adequate power for moderate precipitation effects but not for temperature extremes in sparse strata.

papers.title_zh: 2005-2020年中国10省气象因素与肾综合征出血热发病率:两阶段、年龄分层分布滞后非线性分析
papers.source_body_en: Abstract Background Haemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS) is a rodent-borne zoonosis with its largest burden in China. Meteorological conditions influence transmission, but age- and endemic-type-specific associations remain unclear, and most multi-region studies lack population denominators. Methods We analysed 132,313 age-stratified HFRS cases reported during 2005–2020 in ten Chinese provinces, grouped by reservoir-host seasonality into Apodemus-type, Mixed-type and Rattus-type regions. Population denominators came from three censuses and revised intercensal series; monthly meteorological exposures came from quality-controlled national stations. Within each province and age stratum (0–19, 20–59, ≥ 60 years), we fitted quasi-Poisson distributed lag non-linear models (lag 0–6 months) with a log person-month offset and mutual exposure adjustment, pooling reduced curves by endemic type and stratum. Curve robustness was assessed using best linear unbiased predictions and a 2,000-draw bootstrap; null results were bounded by minimum detectable relative risks; provincial covariates were examined in meta-regressions. Results The 20–59-year stratum contributed 75.8% of cases (annual incidence 1.70 per 100,000, versus 0.33 at 0–19 and 1.57 at ≥ 60 years). In Apodemus-type provinces, precipitation showed an inverted-U association peaking at 175.9 mm (relative risk (RR) 2.73, 95% CI 1.44–5.18), strongest at ages 20–59 (190.6 mm, RR 3.08, 1.14–8.37) and robust to leave-one-province-out analysis (95th-percentile RR 1.44–3.52). Temperature peaked near 8.7°C (RR 1.44, 0.34–6.01). Humidity associations were weak on average but diverged across climate zones (dry-promoting in Shaanxi versus humid-promoting in Shandong), producing near-flat pooled curves (I2 up to 72.8%). The two Rattus-type provinces showed opposite temperature-curve directions (heat-promoting in subtropical Yunnan, cold-promoting in temperate Hebei) and are therefore reported per province. Age stratification eliminated Apodemus-type precipitation heterogeneity in the 0–19 and ≥ 60 strata (I2 = 0%). Provincial ageing rate explained temperature-curve heterogeneity (P = 0.004; I2 reduced from 60.0% to 40.2%). Detectability bounds indicated adequate power for moderate precipitation effects at working ages, but not for temperature extremes in sparse strata. Conclusions Meteorological–HFRS associations are structured by reservoir-host endemic type, concentrated in the working-age population, and modified by population ageing. Age-stratified designs with population denominators are essential for unbiased multi-region synthesis.

papers.title: IDENTIFICATION OF A STRUCTURALLY AND EVOLUTIONARILY CONSERVED 3'→5' PROOFREADING EXONUCLEASE DOMAIN IN THE LARGE L PROTEIN OF HANTAVIRUSES- EMERGING HUMAN PATHOGENS
papers.abstract: The proofreading 3′→5′ exonuclease not only represents a crucial class of enzymes responsible for maintaining genome integrity across diverse groups of organisms, but also plays a critical role in ensuring replication fidelity. In the non-segmented, positive-strand bat-borne RNA viruses like Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome Coronaviruses (SARS-CoVs and MERS-CoV), it is found along with the methyltransferase (MTase) gene of the non-structural protein 14 (NSP14). In contrast, in the non-segmented, but negative-strand bat-borne RNA viruses such as Marburg, Ebola and Nipah viruses, it has been identified together with a novel type of capping enzyme, viz. guanosine diphosphate polyribonucleotidyltransferase (PRNTase). Hantaviruses, one of the fatal and emerging human pathogens in recent times, belong to segmented, negative-strand RNA viruses and are primarily rodent-borne. Currently, no universally approved vaccine or antiviral therapy exists for all hantavirus infections. The presence of a proofreading (PR) exonuclease domain has not been reported in hantaviruses until now. Interestingly, a putative PR exonuclease domain has been identified for the first time in these viruses within the large L protein, preceding the RNA-dependent RNA polymerase (RdRp). The newly identified domain belongs to the DEDD superfamily, but exhibits a distinct structural deviation, notably the replacement of the first catalytic triad -DxE- in the Old World hantaviruses with an -NxE- motif in most of the New World hantaviruses, and the use of an invariant tyrosine instead of histidine at the proton acceptor site. This feature closely resembles the DEDD superfamily of PR exonucleases reported in bacterial DNA polymerases I and II and in the DNA-dependent DNA polymerases of DNA viruses. To the best of my knowledge, this study provides the first evidence for the presence of a typical DEDD superfamily of PR exonuclease domain in hantaviruses, and thus, expanding our understanding of the structure and catalytic mechanism of 3′→5′ PR exonucleases in segmented, negative-strand RNA viruses and further presenting a novel structural target for the development of universally effective antiviral therapies against fatal hantavirus infections.

analysis.methods: The study identified a putative PR exonuclease domain in the large L protein of hantaviruses through sequence analysis. It compared the domain's structure with known DEDD superfamily members and noted specific deviations in the catalytic triad and proton acceptor site.
analysis.main_results: The presence of a proofreading (PR) exonuclease domain in hantaviruses has not been previously reported. This domain was identified within the large L protein, preceding the RNA-dependent RNA polymerase (RdRp).

However, the study is limited to sequence analysis without experimental validation, resulting in moderate evidence strength.

elements_zh.methods: 该研究通过序列分析,在汉坦病毒的大 L 蛋白中鉴定出了一个假定的 PR 核酸外切酶结构域。它将该结构域的结构与已知的 DEDD 超家族成员进行了比较,并注意到催化三联体和质子受体位点的特定偏差。
elements_zh.main_results: 此前尚未报道过汉坦病毒中存在校对 (PR) 核酸外切酶结构域。该结构域位于大 L 蛋白内,位于 RNA 依赖性 RNA 聚合酶 (RdRp) 之前。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 该研究首次提供了汉坦病毒中PR外切酶结构域典型DEDD超家族的证据,拓展了我们对分段负链RNA病毒中3′→5′PR外切酶结构和催化机制的理解。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这一发现为开发针对致命性汉坦病毒感染的普遍有效的 抗病毒药物 疗法提供了一个新的结构靶标,这可能对 治疗 和预防策略产生重大影响。

The newly identified domain belongs to the DEDD superfamily, but exhibits a distinct structural deviation, notably the replacement of the first catalytic triad -DxE- in the Old World hantaviruses with an -NxE- motif in most of the New World hantaviruses, and the use of an invariant tyrosine instead of histidine at the proton acceptor site. This feature closely resembles the DEDD superfamily of PR exonucleases reported in bacterial DNA polymerases I and II and in the DNA-dependent DNA polymerases of DNA viruses.
