analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在研究 汉坦病毒(新兴的人类病原体)中 3′→5′ 校对核酸外切酶结构域的结构和进化保守性。这项研究的动机是需要了解这些病毒中 基因组 完整性和复制保真度的分子机制。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究的重点是 汉坦病毒,这是一种主要由啮齿动物传播的分段负链 RNA 病毒。它检查了汉坦病毒大 L 蛋白中是否存在校对核酸外切酶结构域,特别是在其结构和进化特征的背景下。
analysis_zh.methods: 该研究通过序列分析,在汉坦病毒的大 L 蛋白中鉴定出了一个假定的 PR 核酸外切酶结构域。它将该结构域的结构与已知的 DEDD 超家族成员进行了比较,并注意到催化三联体和质子受体位点的特定偏差。
analysis_zh.main_results: 此前尚未报道过汉坦病毒中存在校对 (PR) 核酸外切酶结构域。该结构域位于大 L 蛋白内,位于 RNA 依赖性 RNA 聚合酶 (RdRp) 之前。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 该研究首次提供了汉坦病毒中PR外切酶结构域典型DEDD超家族的证据,拓展了我们对分段负链RNA病毒中3′→5′PR外切酶结构和催化机制的理解。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这一发现为开发针对致命性汉坦病毒感染的普遍有效的 抗病毒药物 疗法提供了一个新的结构靶标,这可能对 治疗 和预防策略产生重大影响。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究基于序列分析,并未提供核酸外切酶活性的实验验证。证据是温和的,因为它依赖于比较基因组数据而没有功能测定。

papers.title: Serologically analyzing blood samples from Mongolian livestock for zoonotic pathogens
papers.abstract: Mongolia faces a significant risk from zoonotic diseases including tick-borne encephalitis virus (TBEV), Crimean-Congo hemorrhagic fever virus (CCHFV), Hantaan virus (HTNV), and Yersinia pestis due to its large livestock and pastoralist populations. Given the potential exposure risk from infected livestock for Mongolian herders and military personnel transiting on operation, we sought to characterize seroprevalence rates among livestock animals against these high-consequence vector-borne and rodent-borne diseases. Whole blood samples were collected from cattle, goat, horse, sheep, and camel from 2014 to 2015 in three aimags (provinces): Tuv, Selenge, and Dornogovi. Samples were tested for reactive antibodies against these pathogens using the MAGPIX ® system and an in-house multiplex assay. Based on an optimized 20-fold signal-to-noise threshold cutoff, the following positivity rates were detected: in Tuv- 0% (HTNV), 1.4% (TBEV), 0.5% ( Y. pestis ) and 0% (CCHFV); in Selenge- 0.6% (HTNV), 3.2% (TBEV), 0% ( Y. pestis ), and 0.3% (CCHFV); and in Dornogovi- 0.2% (HTNV), 0.7% (TBEV), 1.3% ( Y. pestis ), and 1.7% (CCHFV). The highest positivity by pathogen and animal group was observed for TBEV in horses from Selenge (9.4%) and CCHFV in camels from Dornogovi (11.4%). These findings highlight the value of livestock surveillance for identifying circulating zoonotic pathogens and assessing public and veterinary health risk in Mongolia.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Mongolia faces a significant risk from zoonotic diseases including tick-borne encephalitis virus (TBEV), Crimean-Congo hemorrhagic fever virus (CCHFV), Hantaan virus (HTNV), and Yersinia pestis due to its large livestock and pastoralist populations.
analysis.study_design_and_population: Whole blood samples were collected from cattle, goat, horse, sheep, and camel from 2014 to 2015 in three aimags (provinces): Tuv, Selenge, and Dornogovi.
analysis.methods: Samples were tested for reactive antibodies against these pathogens using the MAGPIX ® system and an in-house multiplex assay.
analysis.main_results: Based on an optimized 20-fold signal-to-noise threshold cutoff, the following positivity rates were detected: in Tuv- 0% (HTNV), 1.4% (TBEV), 0.5% (Y. pestis) and 0% (CCHFV); in Selenge- 0.6% (HTNV), 3.2% (TBEV), 0% (Y. pestis), and 0.3% (CCHFV); and in Dornogovi- 0.2% (HTNV), 0.7% (TBEV), 1.3% (Y. pestis), and 1.7% (CCHFV). analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: These findings highlight the value of livestock surveillance for identifying circulating zoonotic pathogens and assessing public and veterinary health risk in Mongolia.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings can inform targeted surveillance and risk assessment strategies for hantaviruses and other zoonotic pathogens in Mongolia, particularly for livestock that may serve as reservoirs or vectors.

analysis.summary_en: This study aimed to characterize seroprevalence rates of hantaviruses and other zoonotic pathogens among livestock in Mongolia. Blood samples from cattle, goat, horse, sheep, and camel were collected between 2014 and 2015 in three provinces and tested for reactive antibodies using the MAGPIX ® system and an in-house multiplex assay. The results showed varying positivity rates for Hantaan virus (HTNV), tick-borne encephalitis virus (TBEV), and Crimean-Congo hemorrhagic fever virus (CCHFV), with the highest rates observed in horses for TBEV and camels for CCHFV. These findings underscore the importance of livestock surveillance in identifying circulating zoonotic pathogens and assessing public and veterinary health risks in Mongolia. However, the study is limited by its focus on seroprevalence and the single time period of data collection, which may affect the generalisability of the results. The evidence is moderate in strength due to the abstract-only nature of the report and the absence of detailed statistical analysis.

papers.title: Prediction of Quercetin as a Potential Modulator of HTNV-Related Host Responses: An Integrated Computational Study with Baseline Pharmacological Characterization
papers.abstract: Hantaan virus (HTNV) is a rodent-borne zoonotic pathogen that is mainly distributed in East Asia. It is a typical example of a One Health challenge, because it persists in rodent reservoirs without causing disease in the animals but causes severe hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS) when it infects humans. This study employed an integrated bioinformatics approach to systematically identify early-stage HTNV-related host interaction factors, screen potential natural compounds, and predict their underlying therapeutic mechanisms. Integrative bioinformatics analysis identified CXCL10, STAT1, and IL10 as the principal upregulated core genes associated with early-stage HTNV infection. Based on these targets, six candidate natural compounds were retrieved from the HERB database. Notably, quercetin emerged as the most promising candidate, exhibiting a favorable pharmacological profile characterized by high predicted gastrointestinal absorption and an acceptable predicted toxicity profile based on in silico ADMET assessment. Functional enrichment of HTNV-related host interaction targets suggested that HTNV infection may affect multiple host pathways, including HIF-1 signaling. Network pharmacology studies suggest that quercetin may inhibit the damage caused by HTNV infection in the host by regulating the host interaction genes and related pathways associated with HTNV. Combined transcriptomic and database analyses further suggested that quercetin may modulate apoptosis through targets including AKT1, BCL2, and STAT3. In baseline pharmacological assays in uninfected HEK293T cells, quercetin showed low cytotoxicity between 3.90625 and 7.8125 μM, increased cell viability, and reduced transcription of BCL2, MAPK3, and TNF. Molecular docking predicted favorable binding poses of quercetin within HTNV RNA-dependent RNA polymerase (RdRp), with Lys884 and Arg892 as predicted contact residues. In conclusion, these findings identify quercetin as a hypothesis-generating computational candidate for modulating HTNV-related host responses, pending experimental validation. This research framework can provide mechanistic hypotheses regarding host–pathogen interactions and potential intervention targets, thereby supporting the prevention and control of HTNV within the “One Health” framework.

analysis.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to identify potential modulators of HTNV-related host responses and address the challenge of understanding how HTNV interacts with human hosts to cause severe hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS).
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study was a computational analysis using an integrated bioinformatics approach to identify early-stage HTNV-related host interaction factors and screen potential natural compounds. It focused on HTNV infection and its associated host responses.
analysis.methods: The study used integrative bioinformatics analysis, transcriptomic data, and database screening to identify host interaction factors and potential natural compounds. It also included molecular docking and baseline pharmacological assays in uninfected HEK293T cells.
analysis.main_results: Integrative bioinformatics analysis identified CXCL10, STAT1, and IL10 as principal upregulated core genes associated with early-stage HTNV infection. Baseline pharmacological assays showed quercetin had low cytotoxicity and reduced transcription of BCL2, MAPK3, and TNF.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted that quercetin may modulate apoptosis through targets like AKT1, BCL2, and STAT3, and could inhibit HTNV-induced damage by regulating host interaction genes and pathways. This is a novel computational hypothesis for potential therapeutic intervention.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings provide mechanistic hypotheses for host–pathogen interactions and potential intervention targets, supporting the prevention and control of HTNV within the One Health framework.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is based on computational and in silico methods, which may not fully capture biological complexity. The evidence is moderate, as it relies on predictive models and lacks experimental validation.

analysis.summary_en: This study aimed to identify potential modulators of HTNV-related host responses and address the challenge of understanding how HTNV interacts with human hosts to cause severe hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS). The research employed an integrated bioinformatics approach to systematically identify early-stage HTNV-related host interaction factors, screen potential natural compounds, and predict their underlying therapeutic mechanisms. Integrative bioinformatics analysis identified CXCL10, STAT1, and IL10 as principal upregulated core genes associated with early-stage HTNV infection. Baseline pharmacological assays showed quercetin had low cytotoxicity and reduced transcription of BCL2, MAPK3, and TNF. The authors interpreted that quercetin may modulate apoptosis through targets like AKT1, BCL2, and STAT3, and could inhibit HTNV-induced damage by regulating host interaction genes and pathways. This is a novel computational hypothesis for potential therapeutic intervention. The findings provide mechanistic hypotheses for host–pathogen interactions and potential intervention targets, supporting the prevention and control of HTNV within the One Health framework. The study is based on computational and in silico methods, which may not fully capture biological complexity, and the evidence is moderate as it lacks experimental validation.

elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究是一项计算分析,使用综合生物信息学方法来识别早期 HTNV 相关的 宿主 相互作用因子并筛选潜在的天然化合物。它重点关注 HTNV 感染及其相关的 宿主 反应。
elements_zh.methods: 该研究利用综合生物信息学分析、转录组数据和数据库筛选来识别 宿主 相互作用因子和潜在的天然化合物。它还包括未感染的 HEK293T 细胞的分子对接和基线药理学测定。
elements_zh.main_results: 综合生物信息学分析确定 CXCL10、STAT1 和 IL10 是与早期 HTNV 感染相关的主要上调核心基因。基线药理学测定显示槲皮素具有低细胞毒性并减少 BCL2、MAPK3 和 TNF 的转录。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者解释说,槲皮素可能通过 AKT1、BCL2 和 STAT3 等靶标调节细胞凋亡,并可以通过调节 宿主 相互作用基因和通路来抑制 HTNV 诱导的损伤。这是潜在治疗干预的新颖计算假设。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果为 宿主 与病原体相互作用和潜在干预目标提供了机制假设,支持在“同一个健康”框架内预防和控制 HTNV。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究基于计算和计算机方法,可能无法完全捕捉生物的复杂性。证据是温和的,因为它依赖于预测模型并且缺乏实验验证。

papers.title_zh: 槲皮素作为 HTNV 相关 宿主 反应的潜在调节剂的预测:具有基线药理学特征的综合计算研究
papers.source_body_en: Hantaan virus (HTNV) is a rodent-borne zoonotic pathogen that is mainly distributed in East Asia. It is a typical example of a One Health challenge, because it persists in rodent reservoirs without causing disease in the animals but causes severe hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS) when it infects humans. This study employed an integrated bioinformatics approach to systematically identify early-stage HTNV-related host interaction factors, screen potential natural compounds, and predict their underlying therapeutic mechanisms. Integrative bioinformatics analysis identified CXCL10, STAT1, and IL10 as the principal upregulated core genes associated with early-stage HTNV infection. Based on these targets, six candidate natural compounds were retrieved from the HERB database. Notably, quercetin emerged as the most promising candidate, exhibiting a favorable pharmacological profile characterized by high predicted gastrointestinal absorption and an acceptable predicted toxicity profile based on in silico ADMET assessment. Functional enrichment of HTNV-related host interaction targets suggested that HTNV infection may affect multiple host pathways, including HIF-1 signaling. Network pharmacology studies suggest that quercetin may inhibit the damage caused by HTNV infection in the host by regulating the host interaction genes and related pathways associated with HTNV. Combined transcriptomic and database analyses further suggested that quercetin may modulate apoptosis through targets including AKT1, BCL2, and STAT3. In baseline pharmacological assays in uninfected HEK293T cells, quercetin showed low cytotoxicity between 3.90625 and 7.8125 μM, increased cell viability, and reduced transcription of BCL2, MAPK3, and TNF. Molecular docking predicted favorable binding poses of quercetin within HTNV RNA-dependent RNA polymerase (RdRp), with Lys884 and Arg892 as predicted contact residues. In conclusion, these findings identify quercetin as a hypothesis-generating computational candidate for modulating HTNV-related host responses, pending experimental validation. This research framework can provide mechanistic hypotheses regarding host–pathogen interactions and potential intervention targets, thereby supporting the prevention and control of HTNV within the “One Health” framework.
papers.abstract_zh: 汉滩病毒(HTNV)是一种啮齿类动物传播的人畜共患病原体,主要分布在东亚。它是 One Health 挑战的典型例子,因为它在啮齿动物 储存宿主 中持续存在,不会引起动物疾病,但当它感染人类时,会导致严重的 肾综合征出血热 (HFRS)。本研究采用综合生物信息学方法系统地识别早期 HTNV 相关的 宿主 相互作用因子,筛选潜在的天然化合物,并预测其潜在的治疗机制。综合生物信息学分析确定CXCL10、STAT1和IL10是与早期HTNV感染相关的主要上调核心基因。基于这些目标,从 HERB 数据库中检索到了六种候选天然化合物。值得注意的是,槲皮素成为最有前途的候选者,表现出良好的药理学特征,其特征是高预测胃肠道吸收和基于计算机 ADMET 评估的可接受的预测毒性特征。HTNV 相关 宿主 相互作用靶点的功能富集表明 HTNV 感染可能影响多种 宿主 通路,包括 HIF-1 信号传导。网络药理学研究表明,槲皮素可能通过调节宿主相互作用基因以及与HTNV相关的相关通路,抑制HTNV感染对宿主造成的损害。结合转录组学和数据库分析进一步表明,槲皮素可能通过 AKT1、BCL2 和 STAT3 等靶标调节细胞凋亡。在未感染 HEK293T 细胞的基线药理学测定中,槲皮素显示出 3.90625 至 7.8125 μM 之间的低细胞毒性,增加细胞活力,并减少 BCL2、MAPK3 和 TNF 的转录。分子对接预测槲皮素在 HTNV RNA 依赖性 RNA 聚合酶 (RdRp) 内的有利结合姿势,其中 Lys884 和 Arg892 作为预测的接触残基。总之,这些发现将槲皮素确定为一种用于调节 HTNV 相关 宿主 反应的假设生成计算候选物,有待实验验证。该研究框架可以提供有关宿主与病原体相互作用和潜在干预目标的机制假设,从而支持“同一个健康”框架内HTNV的预防和控制。

news.content: 10 14.5M 1.2K Advertisement|Remove ads. A hantavirus outbreak aboard a cruise ship has resulted in three deaths and raised global health concerns. Hundreds of people watch as the cruise ship "Disney Adventure" sets sail in the southwestern Baltic Sea, Germany, on September 01, 2025. (Photo by Jens Büttner/picture alliance via Getty Images) - WHO said affected passengers developed symptoms ranging from fever and stomach issues to severe respiratory complications. - Carnival, Norwegian Cruise Line, and Royal Caribbean declined by up to 1% overnight. - The CDC classified the hantavirus outbreak as a low-level Level 3 emergency response. U.S. cruise stocks, including Carnival (CCL), Norwegian Cruise Line (NCLH), and Royal Caribbean (RCL), all slipped overnight, causing investor concern after a sudden health scare linked to a South Atlantic voyage rattled confidence in an already sensitivity-prone travel sector. A luxury cruise voyage has turned into a major health incident after a hantavirus outbreak aboard the MV Hondius led to three deaths and growing international concern. According to the World Health Organization (WHO), a cluster of acute respiratory illness cases was first flagged on May 2, involving passengers on a cruise ship carrying 147 people. The vessel, which departed Ushuaia, Argentina, in early April, has been anchored off Cabo Verde as authorities coordinate response efforts. WHO noted that symptoms among affected passengers developed between April 6 and April 28, beginning with fever and gastrointestinal distress before rapidly escalating into pneumonia, respiratory failure, and shock in severe cases. WHO said hantaviruses usually spread through infected rodents or contaminated areas. In rare cases, the Andes strain can spread between people in close-contact settings such as shared cabins. Despite the severity of the onboard outbreak, the WHO continues to assess the overall global risk as low. Although global risk assessments remain low, the psychological impact on investors has been evident. Cruise operators' stocks, such as Carnival, Norwegian Cruise Line, and Royal Caribbean, declined by up to 1% overnight after a 2% to 3% decline in the regular session. For many investors, the situation parallels the COVID-19 pandemic, which upended the entire travel industry. Though the U.S. cruise sector has largely recovered from the operational collapse caused by the COVID-19 pandemic, the industry’s largest operators continue to grapple with the long-term consequences of massive borrowing accumulated during the shutdown years. While Royal Caribbean has emerged as the standout performer with returns exceeding 233% over the past five years, rivals CCL and NCLH continue to battle elevated debt burdens and margin pressure. NCLH, in particular, has plunged nearly 40% over the last five years. To make matters worse, last week the company warned that softer travel demand and geopolitical uncertainty are weighing on bookings in key markets and unveiled additional cost-cutting measures to stabilize profits. However, according to a Reuters report, the U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention has categorized the hantavirus outbreak as a Level 3 emergency response, its lowest emergency alert level. So far this year, NCLH and CCL stocks have plunged nearly 23% and 12%, respectively, while RCL stock has gained 0.7%. For updates and corrections, email newsroom[at]stocktwits[dot]com. Trump holds a press conference announcing U.S. Vice President Mike Pence to lead the effort combating the spread of the coronavirus on February 26, 2020. (Photo by Yasin Ozturk/Anadolu Agency via Getty Images) - Trump said that the administration will release a full report on a Hantavirus on Friday. - The outbreak aboard the Dutch-flagged cruise ship Hondius has resulted in three deaths, six confirmed infections and additional suspected cases. - Moderna drew attention due to its hantavirus vaccine partnership with Korea University. Shares of vaccine makers and biodefense companies rallied overnight on Friday after U.S. President Donald Trump addressed a deadly hantavirus outbreak aboard a cruise ship and promised a full update on the situation. Overnight, Emergent BioSolutions (EBS) climbed 3%, while Inovio Pharmaceuticals (INO) and Novavax (NVAX) each gained 2% and Moderna (MRNA) rose 1%. Trump said late Thursday that the administration was closely studying the outbreak from the Dutch-flagged cruise ship Hondius, where three passengers have died and several others became infected. “It’s very much, we hope, under control,” Trump said, adding that a full report will be released on Friday. The outbreak has triggered six confirmed infections and additional suspected cases aboard the vessel, which had 150 passengers onboard during an Atlantic voyage from Argentina toward Europe. Authorities are still investigating how the virus spread on board. Singapore has already isolated two passengers from the ship due to concerns about possible exposure during the trip. The World Health Organization (WHO) also issued an alert on the outbreak, although officials said that the global risk remains low and that hantavirus is less transmissible than COVID-19 or influenza. The virus involved is said to be the Andes strain, one of the few hantavirus variants associated with limited human-to-human transmission. Moderna is viewed as one of the U.S. government’s key vaccine platforms for outbreaks. Since 2023, the company has worked with Korea University’s Vaccine Innovation Center on an mRNA-based hantavirus vaccine candidate, with preclinical studies earlier this year showing protection against hantavirus infection in mice. In 2024, Moderna received a $176 million award backed by the Biomedical Advanced Research and Development Authority (BARDA) in 2024 for the development of mRNA-based pandemic influenza vaccines and outbreak preparedness programs. Moderna’s partnership with the Coalition for Epidemic Preparedness Innovations (CEPI) is also in focus, which previously said mRNA could help shorten vaccine-development timelines to as little as 100 days during outbreaks. Inovio, meanwhile, has the clearest hantavirus link among the stocks rallying overnight. The company previously participated in several hantavirus DNA vaccine studies targeting Hantaan, Puumala and Andes hantavirus strains. One National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases-backed study evaluated an Andes virus DNA vaccine to prevent hantavirus pulmonary syndrome, while another U.S. Army-supported study examined mixed hantavirus DNA vaccines. While none of Inovio’s hantavirus vaccine programs produced a commercial product, the outbreak revived speculative interest in companies with prior hantavirus research. Investors frequently rotate into Novavax during virus headlines due to the company’s vaccine-development platform and history of rapidly developing candidates for pathogens such as Ebola, MERS and Zika. The company’s protein-based nanoparticle platform and Matrix-M adjuvant tech can generate vaccine candidates against emerging infectious diseases, already used in marketed COVID-19 and malaria vaccines. Emergent BioSolutions, on the other hand, is often viewed as one of the U.S. government’s primary biodefense and medical-countermeasure contractors during public-health emergencies. The company has existing relationships with BARDA and makes products based on Anthrax, Ebola, smallpox, mpox and viral hemorrhagic fevers. Emergent previously received BARDA task orders for viral hemorrhagic fever therapeutics and has also participated in manufacturing efforts during outbreaks, including Ebola and Zika. On Stocktwits, retail sentiment for INO and NVAX was ‘extremely bullish’ amid ‘extremely high’ message volume, while MRNA saw ‘bullish’ sentiment with ‘high’ message volume. EBS also recorded ‘extremely bullish’ sentiment, though message volume remained ‘normal.’ Over the past year, MRNA has surged 102%, followed by EBS up 93% and NVAX higher by 55%, while INO has declined 22%. In this photo illustration, a smartphone displays the logo of Datadog, Inc.(Photo illustration by Cheng Xin/Getty Images) - Datadog’s customer usage is growing at the fastest rate since early 2022. - Jefferies, Stifel, and Evercore ISI raised their price targets after Q1 earnings. - Jefferies kept a Buy rating, citing the strongest customer usage growth since early 2022. Datadog, Inc.’s stock (DDOG) is on track to notch its best weekly performance on record as the cloud company delivered a breakout first-quarter (Q1) earnings that ignited investor enthusiasm and underscored its key role in the artificial intelligence infrastructure boom. The stock is also set to be the biggest winner this week on the Nasdaq-100 and the second-best performer on the S&P 500. Jefferies, Stifel and Evercore ISI all raised their price targets on Datadog after what analysts broadly described as a solid “beat and raise” quarter. The firms cited stronger-than-anticipated demand, improving guidance and continued momentum in both core and AI-related products. Jefferies raised its price target on DDOG to $210 from $170 and kept a ‘Buy’ rating, according to TheFly. The firm said customer usage grew at its fastest rate since early 2022, showing strong momentum in its main platform services. Stifel made a more aggressive revision, raising its target to $305 from $160 and also reiterating a ‘Buy’ rating. The firm emphasized that revenue growth continued to pick up sequentially. The new price target implies a 61% upside from the stock’s closing price on Thursday. Evercore ISI also raised its price target to $225 from $175, maintaining an Outperform rating. The firm said the company’s quarterly results and forward guidance helped ease concerns that growth might slow later in the year. Datadog stock traded over 1% lower overnight late Thursday, after surging over 31% in the regular session. In Q1, Datadog posted revenue of $1.006 billion, reaching its first-ever billion-dollar mark and beating analyst expectations of $959.9 million. Adjusted earnings per share came in at $0.60, well above the $0.51 Street forecast, according to Fiscal AI data. The company continued to deepen its enterprise base, growing to roughly 4,550 customers generating more than $100,000 in annual recurring revenue, up from about 3,770 a year earlier. Looking ahead, the company sees Q2 revenue between $1.07 billion and $1.08 billion and EPS between $0.57 and $0.59, compared with the Street estimates of $1.06 billion and $0.58, respectively. On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around the stock remained in ‘extremely bullish’ territory with 1,377% surge in message volume over 24 hours. A user said, “$DDOG earnings just proved high-value SaaS isn’t dying because of AI, it’s accelerating.” Another user said, “damn, I missed this one. Crushing growth with expanding margins.” DDOG stock has gained over 38% year-to-date. The CoreWeave logo is displayed on a mobile phone in this photo illustration in Brussels, Belgium, on November 10, 2025. (Photo by Jonathan Raa/NurPhoto via Getty Images) - CoreWeave’s revenue in Q1 more than doubled and surpassed analysts' expectations; Q2 forecast was softer than expected. - CoreWeave said 2026 capital expenditures would be higher than it had projected earlier. - CRWV stock dropped 10% in post-market hours; retail sentiment moved sharply upward, to ‘extremely bullish.’ CoreWeave, Inc. forecast second-quarter revenue below analysts’ expectations and said its capital expenditure this year would be higher than previously forecast due to increasing component prices, triggering a selloff in shares. Still, retail traders returned upbeat, citing growth prospects and calling the dip an overreaction. CRWV dropped 10% in overnight trading heading into Friday. If the move holds in the regular session, it would mark the worst single-day drop in about a month. CoreWeave’s quarterly report forced investors to reassess their outlook on the company, as strong revenue and order growth were accompanied by sharply rising expenses. In recent months, Meta Platforms committed $21 billion for CoreWeave’s cloud capacity through 2032, with the cloud operator also signing new multi-billion-dollar deals with Anthropic and Jane Street. Demand for the so-called neocloud providers such as CoreWeave and Nebius has surged over the last year as tech companies race to secure the hardware and cloud capacity to support AI development and user growth. Microsoft, OpenAI, Meta, and Nvidia are among CoreWeave's largest customers. The company’s total revenue surged 105% to $2.08 billion in the first quarter, beating analysts’ estimate of $1.97 billion from LSEG/Reuters. Operating expenses more than doubled to $2.22 billion, a result of continuing to scale active power capacity. Backlog, which denotes orders booked but not yet realized as revenue, jumped to $99.4 billion as of March 31, compared with $66.8 billion at the end of December. Last quarter, CoreWeave added more than 400 megawatts of contracted power, bringing its total to more than 3.5 gigawatts. For Q2, the company expects revenue in the range of $2.45 billion to $2.6 billion, below analysts' estimate of $2.69 billion. The focus item, still, was the capital expenditure. Not only did CoreWeave's capex increased 90% sequentially to $7.70 billion in Q1, but the company also said the 2026 figure would be slightly higher. The company now expects full-year capital expenditures in a range of $31 billion to $35 billion, up from a previous low end of $30 billion. “In the last six, nine months, there has been an acute shortage of certain components that have moved up,” CEO Michael Intrator said on the analyst call, adding that the structure of its supply contracts offers the company some insulation from price volatility. On Stocktwits, the retail sentiment for CRWV flipped to ‘extremely bullish’ from ‘neutral’ the previous day. “Buying Coreweave now is similar to buying csco in 1989 or cell tower company AMT in 2001 at 1.00,” a trader said, signaling that it's still early days for neocloud companies and the upside potential is huge. “Everybody is worried about today's debt. Well 8 years ago the Oilers gave McDavid 12 million a year. Today that contract looks mighty savy... I think it's bullcrap this stock will be fine with NVDA backing and Blackstone owning notes.” Another wrote: “CoreWeave’s sell-off is a market misread. The business isn’t demand-constrained — the $99.4B backlog proves that.” Still, some traders remained concerned of the growing leverage and bottom-line pressure, with one saying, “losses and debt. This goes below 100 soon enough.” CoreWeave went public in March 2025. The stock has surged 80% this year. Wall Street expects another loss-making quarter, with Koyfin estimates projecting EPS loss to widen to $0.06 from $0.05. SLS stock has surged 188% over the past year. (Photo credit: Getty Images) - Deutsche Bank raised its holdings to 137,646 shares valued at $582,000 in the March quarter. - Sellas’ largest shareholders include Vanguard Group, BlackRock, and State Street, among others. - The company recently took part in discussions on the EU Biotech Act related to drug approvals, biotech competitiveness, and patient access. Shares of Sellas Life Sciences, Inc. (SLS) are poised to end the week in the green as investors increased their bets on the cancer-drug developer and tracked big money ahead of earnings and a potential acute myeloid leukemia (AML) trial catalyst. SLS stock ended Thursday over 4% lower at 4.93, but shares are tracking their best week in nearly a month after gaining about 11% so far this week. Fresh filings showed that Deutsche Bank increased its stake in SLS by 50% during the March quarter. The bank added 45,958 shares, bringing its total holdings to 137,646 shares valued at $582,000, according to data from Quiver Quantitative. The filing came alongside several smaller institutional stakes, including a more than 500% increase from Rothschild Investment, though the stake remains comparatively small at 127 shares. The company’s top shareholders include BlackRock, now the largest investor, with 12.1 million shares valued at $51.3 million as of March 31, up from 7.54 million shares valued at $28.4 million at the end of last year, per Fiscal AI data. As of the end of last year, Vanguard Group held 8.5 million shares valued at $35.8 million. Geode Capital Management held shares valued at about $13 million, while State Street held a stake valued at $9.3 million. Wall Street expects another loss-making quarter as Sellas continues investing heavily in clinical development and pipeline expansion. According to Koyfin estimates, analysts expect a loss per share (EPS) of $0.06 for the quarter, compared with a loss of $0.05 in the prior quarter. Earnings before interest and taxes (EBIT) is projected to widen to $9 million from about $8.3 million previously. According to Koyfin data, Sellas carries a 12-month average analyst price target of $10, implying an upside of 103% from current levels. CoreWeave’s quarterly report forced investors to reassess their outlook on the company, as strong revenue and order growth were accompanied by sharply rising expenses. In recent months, Meta Platforms committed $21 billion for CoreWeave’s cloud capacity through 2032, with the cloud operator also signing new multi-billion-dollar deals with Anthropic and Jane Street. Demand for the so-called neocloud providers such as CoreWeave and Nebius has surged over the last year as tech companies race to secure the hardware and cloud capacity to support AI development and user growth. Microsoft, OpenAI, Meta, and Nvidia are among CoreWeave's largest customers. The company’s total revenue surged 105% to $2.08 billion in the first quarter, beating analysts’ estimate of $1.97 billion from LSEG/Reuters. Operating expenses more than doubled to $2.22 billion, a result of continuing to scale active power capacity. Backlog, which denotes orders booked but not yet realized as revenue, jumped to $99.4 billion as of March 31, compared with $66.8 billion at the end of December. Last quarter, CoreWeave added more than 400 megawatts of contracted power, bringing its total to more than 3.5 gigawatts. For Q2, the company expects revenue in the range of $2.45 billion to $2.6 billion, below analysts' estimate of $2.69 billion. The focus item, still, was the capital expenditure. Not only did CoreWeave's capex increased 90% sequentially to $7.70 billion in Q1, but the company also said the 2026 figure would be slightly higher. The company now expects full-year capital expenditures in a range of $31 billion to $35 billion, up from a previous low end of $30 billion. “In the last six, nine months, there has been an acute shortage of certain components that have moved up,” CEO Michael Intrator said on the analyst call, adding that the structure of its supply contracts offers the company some insulation from price volatility. On Stocktwits, the retail sentiment for CRWV flipped to ‘extremely bullish’ from ‘neutral’ the previous day. “Buying Coreweave now is similar to buying csco in 1989 or cell tower company AMT in 2001 at 1.00,” a trader said, signaling that it's still early days for neocloud companies and the upside potential is huge. “Everybody is worried about today's debt. Well 8 years ago the Oilers gave McDavid 12 million a year. Today that contract looks mighty savy... I think it's bullcrap this stock will be fine with NVDA backing and Blackstone owning notes.” Another wrote: “CoreWeave’s sell-off is a market misread. The business isn’t demand-constrained — the $99.4B backlog proves that.” Still, some traders remained concerned of the growing leverage and bottom-line pressure, with one saying, “losses and debt. This goes below 100 soon enough.” CoreWeave went public in March 2025. The stock has surged 80% this year. analysis.brief_en: A hantavirus outbreak on a cruise ship has caused significant concern and economic impact. The outbreak, which began in early April 2025, was first flagged on May 2, 2025, involving 150 passengers on an Atlantic voyage from Argentina toward Europe. The World Health Organization (WHO) reported three deaths, six confirmed infections, and additional suspected cases, with symptoms ranging from fever and gastrointestinal issues to severe respiratory complications. The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) classified the outbreak as a low-level Level 3 emergency response. The WHO stated that the global risk remains low, as hantaviruses are less transmissible than COVID-19 or influenza. The outbreak has led to a decline in cruise stocks, including Carnival (CCL), Norwegian Cruise Line (NCLH), and Royal Caribbean (RCL), with each dropping up to 1% overnight. The U.S. administration, including President Donald Trump, is closely monitoring the situation and plans to release a full report. Authorities are still investigating the transmission route, and the virus involved is the Andes strain, which is associated with limited human-to-human spread. The outbreak has raised fears among investors, who compare it to the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on the travel industry.

news.title: Cryo-EM reveals how Andes hantavirus grips its human cell receptor
news.excerpt: A new Nature study shows that the Andes virus spike captures the PCDH1 receptor through a deep central pocket that most antibodies cannot reach.
news.rss_summary_html: A new Nature study shows that the Andes virus spike captures the PCDH1 receptor through a deep central pocket that most antibodies cannot reach.

news.content_title: Cryo-EM reveals how Andes hantavirus grips its human cell receptor
news.content: HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER Friday, October 30, 2026 No Result View All Result Login HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER No Result View All Result No Result View All Result Home NEWS Science News Health Cryo-EM reveals how Andes hantavirus grips its human cell receptor by October 28, 2026 in Health Reading Time: 4 mins read 0 Cryo-EM reveals how Andes hantavirus grips its human cell receptor Share on FacebookShare on TwitterShare on LinkedinShare on RedditShare on Telegram Scientists at Albert Einstein College of Medicine, working with collaborators at Institut Pasteur and LSU Health Shreveport, have published a study in Nature showing how the Andes hantavirus recognizes its target on a human cell. The work arrives against a sobering backdrop: earlier this year, an outbreak of Andes hantavirus on a cruise ship killed three passengers and sickened 13, underscoring the absence of approved vaccines or treatments for the virus. The new findings, the researchers say, could inform the development of effective therapies against Andes virus and other hantaviruses. Hantaviruses are a large family of viruses carried mainly by rodents, and they can cause serious and sometimes fatal diseases in people, including hantavirus pulmonary syndrome, a severe respiratory illness that can rapidly lead to breathing failure. Human infections occur mainly when people inhale airborne virus particles from the urine, droppings, or saliva of infected rodents. Of the more than 20 hantaviruses known to sicken humans, Andes virus is the only one known to spread from person to person, typically through close and prolonged contact. This year’s cruise ship outbreak provided a dramatic example of that capability. The research team had previously established that infection depends on the spike protein on the Andes virus surface latching onto a receptor called PCDH1 on the surface of human cells. That receptor essentially serves as a doorway for the virus to enter the cell and then multiply inside it. What remained unanswered was a precise mechanistic question: how does the spike protein actually latch onto PCDH1? Eight years ago the group discovered that Andes virus uses this particular surface protein to infect human cells, but the exact recognition mechanism eluded them. “Eight years ago, we discovered that Andes virus infects human cells by using a particular protein on the cell’s surface, called a receptor, but we couldn’t figure out exactly how the virus recognized it,” said co-corresponding author Kartik Chandran, Ph.D., professor of microbiology and immunology at Einstein. “Our latest work solves this puzzle: We reveal a new way in which a virus can capture its receptor during infection and also suggest how we can fight back with therapies targeted to exploit the resulting viral vulnerability.” The answer lies in an unusual architecture. The spike protein of SARS-CoV-2, the virus that causes COVID-19, is built from three identical protein units arranged in a triangle, each carrying a separate receptor-binding domain that latches onto its receptor, ACE2. The Andes virus spike, by contrast, is an arrangement of four identical protein units locked together into a square. Unlike the SARS-CoV-2 and ACE2 pairing, a single protein unit from the Andes virus cannot bind to its receptor on its own; instead, the entire square-shaped spike is required to capture PCDH1. To see what happens at the very beginning of infection, when the Andes virus first encounters a human cell, the researchers used cryo-electron microscopy to reveal the structure in sharp detail. That step was accomplished only after the team developed innovative new methods, including an artificial intelligence-designed scaffold, that enabled the square-shaped Andes virus spike to hold together in a test tube. “The best way to prove a rare bird exists is to take a picture of it,” said Pablo Guardado-Calvo, Ph.D., deputy director of the Virology Department and head of the Structural Biology of Infectious Diseases unit at Institut Pasteur. “When we mixed this engineered Andes virus spike with PCDH1 and looked at it under the microscope, we knew we had something special.” The structures showed that a single molecule of PCDH1 embeds itself into the heart of the spike by binding into a deep groove, or pocket, at its center. The researchers also resolved molecular specifics of the interaction that will be important for designing treatments intended to block it. “The depth of this pocket also helps explain how the virus limits antibody access,” said Rohit Jangra, Ph.D., assistant professor of microbiology and immunology at LSU Health Shreveport. “What’s striking is how the same pocket can accommodate the receptor while restricting antibody access. PCDH1’s long, slender shape lets it reach deep inside, but most antibodies are too bulky to follow.” The team then examined several antibodies isolated from human hantavirus patients that had previously been shown to block the Andes virus-PCDH1 binding interaction. They found that some of these antibodies could indeed bind close enough to the entrance of the receptor-binding pocket to prevent PCDH1 from entering it, but they could not fit as deeply into the pocket as PCDH1 does. According to Chandran, this suggests a clever way in which Andes virus can escape receptor-blocking antibodies: the virus mutates so that antibodies cannot destroy it, yet those changes do not affect its ability to bind to the receptor, a kind of molecular “friend-or-foe” identification system. That same antibody-escape strategy, however, creates a vulnerability the team intends to exploit. The new findings, the researchers say, could inform the development of effective therapies against Andes virus and other hantaviruses. Hantaviruses are a large family of viruses carried mainly by rodents, and they can cause serious and sometimes fatal diseases in people, including hantavirus pulmonary syndrome, a severe respiratory illness that can rapidly lead to breathing failure. Human infections occur mainly when people inhale airborne virus particles from the urine, droppings, or saliva of infected rodents. Of the more than 20 hantaviruses known to sicken humans, Andes virus is the only one known to spread from person to person, typically through close and prolonged contact. The research team had previously established that infection depends on the spike protein on the Andes virus surface latching onto a receptor called PCDH1 on the surface of human cells. That receptor essentially serves as a doorway for the virus to enter the cell and then multiply inside it. What remained unanswered was a precise mechanistic question: how does the spike protein actually latch onto PCDH1? Eight years ago the group discovered that Andes virus uses this particular surface protein to infect human cells, but the exact recognition mechanism eluded them. “Eight years ago, we discovered that Andes virus infects human cells by using a particular protein on the cell’s surface, called a receptor, but we couldn’t figure out exactly how the virus recognized it,” said co-corresponding author Kartik Chandran, Ph.D., professor of microbiology and immunology at Einstein. “Our latest work solves this puzzle: We reveal a new way in which a virus can capture its receptor during infection and also suggest how we can fight back with therapies targeted to exploit the resulting viral vulnerability.” The answer lies in an unusual architecture. The spike protein of SARS-CoV-2, the virus that causes COVID-19, is built from three identical protein units arranged in a triangle, each carrying a separate receptor-binding domain that latches onto its receptor, ACE2. The Andes virus spike, by contrast, is an arrangement of four identical protein units locked together into a square. Unlike the SARS-CoV-2 and ACE2 pairing, a single protein unit from the Andes virus cannot bind to its receptor on its own; instead, the entire square-shaped spike is required to capture PCDH1. PCDH1’s long, slender shape lets it reach deep inside, but most antibodies are too bulky to follow.” The team then examined several antibodies isolated from human hantavirus patients that had previously been shown to block the Andes virus-PCDH1 binding interaction. They found that some of these antibodies could indeed bind close enough to the entrance of the receptor-binding pocket to prevent PCDH1 from entering it, but they could not fit as deeply into the pocket as PCDH1 does. According to Chandran, this suggests a clever way in which Andes virus can escape receptor-blocking antibodies: the virus mutates so that antibodies cannot destroy it, yet those changes do not affect its ability to bind to the receptor, a kind of molecular “friend-or-foe” identification system. OffOn Stream on 3 people waiting to be medically evacuated from cruise ship at center of suspected hantavirus outbreak There are currently two laboratory-confirmed and five suspected cases. ByMary Kekatos and Othon Leyva May 6, 2026, 1:06 AM At least three people are waiting to be medically evacuated from a cruise ship at the center of a suspected hantavirus outbreak. As of Monday, there have been seven cases reported aboard the MV Hondius, of which two are laboratory-confirmed and five are suspected. Among those seven, there have been three deaths, including a married couple from the Netherlands, one of whom has been confirmed to have been infected with hantavirus. The ship is currently off the coast of Cape Verde and medical teams have been assessing two staff members and a close contact of one of the deceased patients. Related American speaks out from cruise ship amid deadly hantavirus outbreak Cape Verde officials told ABC News they are checking on what care the three patients need before transferring them to ambulances and then on flights to the Netherlands. Two planes have been arranged for medical evacuations of the sick passengers from the ship between 4 a.m. and 6 a.m. ET, according to World Health Organization representative for Cape Verde Dr. Ann Lindstrand. The vessel is expected to sail to the Spanish island of Tenerife in Spain, where Spanish health authorities will take over further investigations, including lab testing and clinical assessments, particularly for older passengers, according to Cape Verde officials. Jake Rosmarin, an American passenger on the ship, told ABC News that all the remaining passengers on board remain "in good spirits" and "are hopeful that this situation will be resolved soon." "Safety measures are in place, including social distancing and masking. Passengers also have the option to have meals delivered directly to their cabins," he said. "Access to the outer decks is permitted for fresh air, while gathering in indoor common areas such as the lounge is currently restricted." This aerial picture shows a general view of the cruise ship MV Hondius stationary off the port of Praia, the capital of Cape Verde, on May 5, 2026. AFP via Getty Images It comes as an epidemiologist at the WHO said there may be some person-to-person spread in the outbreak. "We do believe that there may be some human-to-human transmission that's happening among the really close contacts, the husband and wife, people who've shared cabins, [et cetera]," Maria Van Kerkhove, an infectious disease epidemiologist and director of Epidemic and Pandemic Management at the WHO, said during a press conference Tuesday. "So again, our assumption is that has happened, and that's why we are operating and working with the ship to make sure that anyone who is symptomatic, anyone caring for patients, is wearing full personal protective equipment," she added. Van Kerkhove noted that hantaviruses normally don't transmit from person to person because it's a "rodent infection." Patients typically become infected when they come into contact with rodent urine, droppings or saliva, according to the WHO. The initial patients who fell ill may have become infected before they boarded the ship, Van Kerkhove added. Symptoms of hantavirus infections sometimes do not start until eight weeks after contact with the virus, according to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention. Related 3 dead in suspected hantavirus outbreak aboard a cruise ship: What to know The WHO is working under the assumption that the strain of hantavirus in the suspected outbreak is the Andes virus, which historically has been shown to potentially transmit between people, although sequencing is still ongoing, according to Van Kerkhove. In a post on its website, the WHO said the onset of illnesses aboard the MV Hondius occurred between April 6 and April 28, with patients experiencing fever, gastrointestinal symptoms, rapid progression to pneumonia, acute respiratory distress syndrome and shock. "The outbreak is being managed through coordinated international response, and includes in-depth investigations, case isolation and care, medical evacuation and laboratory investigations," the WHO wrote in the post. WHO Director-General Dr. Tedros Ghebreysus wrote in a post on X Tuesday that the infection risk to the global population is low and that the agency will continue to monitor the situation and provide updates. Timeline of cases The first suspected hantavirus case occurred in a 70-year-old male passenger from the Netherlands who developed fever, headache and mild diarrhea on April 6, according to the WHO and South African health officials. His body was removed from the ship to the British territory of St. Helena on April 24. No microbiological tests were performed on the man, according to the WHO. Also on April 24, the male passenger's 69-year-old wife developed gastrointestinal symptoms, health officials said. Her health rapidly declined while on a flight to Johannesburg, South Africa, on April 25 and she died upon arrival to an emergency department the next day, the WHO said. WHO epidemic and pandemic preparedness and prevention chief Maria Van Kerkhove speaking regarding hantavirus cases at the WHO heaquarters in Geneva, May 4, 2026. World Health Organization/AFP via Getty Images On Monday, May 4, laboratory testing confirmed that the wife was infected with hantavirus. Health workers have begun working to identify anyone who may have come into contact with the couple. According to the WHO, the couple had traveled in South America, including Argentina, before they boarded the cruise ship on April 1. During Tuesday's press conference, Van Kerkhove said officials suspect the couple was infected with hantavirus before boarding the ship. "The initial patients, the initial case and his wife, they joined the boat in Argentina. And with the timing of the incubation period of hantavirus, which can be anywhere from one to six weeks, our assumption is that they were infected off the ship, perhaps doing some activities there," she said. A British passenger started developing symptoms on April 24, including shortness of breath and signs of pneumonia, according to the WHO and South African health officials. His condition worsened and he was medically evacuated from Ascension, another British territory, to South Africa on April 27, where he is currently hospitalized in an intensive care unit. Laboratory testing confirmed hantavirus infection over the weekend, the WHO said. Another passenger, an adult female, began experiencing symptoms on April 28, including a general feeling of being unwell, according to the WHO. She later presented with pneumonia and died on May 2. Oceanwide Expeditions, which operates the cruise ship, previously revealed that the patient was a German national. In addition, there are three suspected cases currently onboard the MV Hondius reporting high fever and/or gastrointestinal symptoms, the WHO said. The ship is currently off the coast of Cape Verde, where medical teams in the area are evaluating the patients and collecting additional specimens for testing, according to the WHO. Van Kerkhove said the highest priority is to medically evacuate the symptomatic individuals onboard the ship so they receive the care they need. "The plan now is for the ship to continue on to the Canary Islands. We're working with Spanish authorities who will welcome the ship, have said that they will welcome the ship, to do a full investigation, a full epidemiological investigation, full disinfection of the ship, and of course to assess the risk of the passengers that are actually on board," she said. "The medical evacuation of two individuals currently requiring urgent medical care, and the individual associated with the guest who passed away on 2 May, will occur using two specialized aircraft that are en route to Cape Verde," Oceanwide Expeditions said in a statement Tuesday. "From here, the patients are to be medically evacuated to the Netherlands," the statement continued, noting that there currently was no "exact timeline" for the evacuation. The company added that once the guests have been safely transferred and are in transit to the Netherlands, the ship will proceed to the Canary Islands. "[T]he hospital has already prepared an area with isolation capacity, should it be necessary," Angela Gomes, Cape Verde's national director of health, said in a statement Tuesday. "A dedicated team has been formed, with doctors, infectious disease specialists, nurses and laboratory technicians, to support patients on board and, if necessary, also on land." The Spanish Ministry of Health said Spain will host the MV Hondius vessel in the Canary Islands in compliance with "international law and the humanitarian spirit." Once there, crew and passengers will be examined, treated and transferred to their respective countries, the ministry said. Following this same logic, and as part of the operation, the Government has also accepted a formal request from the Government of the Netherlands to take in the doctor from the MV Hondius, who is in serious condition and will be transported to the Canary Islands on a hospital plane today. OffOn Stream on WHO says suspected hantavirus cluster 'is not the start of a COVID pandemic' There are 12 suspected cases so far. ByMary Kekatos and Zoe Magee May 7, 2026, 4:39 PM Share An epidemiologist from the World Health Organization (WHO) said Thursday that the suspected hantavirus cluster aboard a cruise ship is not the beginning of another COVID-19 pandemic. Eight cases are currently being reported by the WHO, including five laboratory-confirmed cases and three suspected cases. Of those eight cases, three have died. Dr. Maria Van Kerkhove, an infectious disease epidemiologist and acting director of epidemic and pandemic management at the WHO, was asked during a press conference what the difference was between this cluster and the early days of the COVID pandemic. Related Officials in Arizona, Georgia monitoring some hantavirus cruise ship passengers who have returned to US "I want to be unequivocal here. This is not SARS-CoV-2. This is not the start of a COVID pandemic. This is an outbreak that we see on a ship," Van Kerkhove said. Van Kerkhove explained that hantavirus doesn't spread in the same way that coronaviruses do, but rather through "close, intimate contact." Most hantaviruses don't transmit from person to person. "The actions that are being taken on board [the ship] are precautionary to prevent any onward spread," she added. Health personnel assisting patients onto a boat from the cruise ship MV Hondius, while stationary off the port of Praia, the capital of Cape Verde, May 6, 2026. AFP via Getty Images There appears to be two confirmed cases and four suspected cases that have not been added to the WHO's official count yet. The Ministry of Health, Welfare and Sport confirmed that two patients infected with the virus are currently hospitalized in the Netherlands, one at Radboud University Medical Center and the other at Leiden University Medical Center. Additionally, two Singapore residents who were on board the ship are currently being monitored. Singapore's Communicable Diseases Agency said it was notified of the individuals on May 4 and 5. "They have been isolated at the National Centre for Infectious Diseases, where they are being tested for hantavirus. The risk to the general public in Singapore is currently low," the agency said. The agency added that test results are pending, with one resident having a runny nose. The other is asymptomatic. The French Health Ministry also issued a statement on Thursday that a French national has been tested after they displayed mild symptoms. This person had been in contact with one of the confirmed cases. Related 3 people waiting to be medically evacuated from cruise ship at center of suspected hantavirus outbreak Three deaths have been recorded so far, including a married Dutch couple. The 70-year-old male patient died on April 11, and his body was taken off the ship on the island of St. Helena on April 24. His 69-year-old wife disembarked on the same day, and her health rapidly deteriorated. She died at a South Africa hospital on April 26. A third passenger, a German woman, presented with pneumonia symptoms starting on April 28, according to the WHO. The woman died on May 2 from causes not yet known, according to Oceanwide Expeditions, which operates the cruise ship. The WHO said 29 people disembarked on St. Helena on the same day that the body of the Dutch male patient and his wife disembarked. They traveled to 12 countries: Canada, Switzerland, Germany, Denmark, Great Britain, St. Kitts and Nevis, Netherlands, New Zealand, Singapore, Sweden, Turkey and the United States. Popular Reads 2 college students found dead after going missing while hiking, police say 17 hours ago 'Inexplicable' order probed as cause of train crash that killed at least 69: Official 6 hours ago Britt McHenry resigns from State Department after basketball game altercation Oct 23 The disembarked guests have all been contacted by Oceanwide Expeditions. In the U.S., local authorities in five states -- Arizona, California, Georgia, Texas and Virginia -- are monitoring the disembarked passengers and are conducting contact tracing, None have shown signs of illness at this time. Anais Legend, technical lead for viral hemorrhagic fevers at WHO, said during the press conference on Thursday that "step-by-step guidance is being developed" for the disembarked passengers and that the WHO is coordinating with national authorities. Anyone with any signs of symptoms will be isolated while other passengers have their risk exposure evaluated. The cruise ship MV Hondius, carrying passengers suspected of having cases of hantavirus on board, leaves Praia, Cape Verde, May 6, 2026. Reuters Public health experts said they expected a more robust response from the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) and the National Institutes of Health. "CDC would typically be asked by WHO to, or by a country to, help in technical assistance," Dr. Carlos del Rio, an H. Cliff Sauls distinguished professor of medicine at the Emory University School of Medicine, told reporters on Thursday. Typically, CDC teams would be deployed to an area, he said, and the teams would perform contact tracing and interviews and conduct an outbreak investigation. "I would envision by now, many, many days ago, we would have seen ... a team from CDC deployed to the area," he added. Related 3 dead in suspected hantavirus outbreak aboard a cruise ship: What to know Dr. Jeanne Marrazzo, CEO of the IDSA, added that she would have expected a CDC press briefing, an alert from the agency's Health Alert Network or information from the NIH on potential treatments in the pipeline that could receive emergency use authorization to help treat hantavirus patients. Marrazzo said she is not aware that conversations about potential therapies at NIH aren't happening but it "does not give me a lot of assurance or reassurance that we're not hearing about any of it." The CDC posted a statement on X on Wednesday on behalf of NIH Director and acting CDC director Dr. Jay Bhattacharya that read, "Our hearts go out to the passengers aboard the cruise ship M/V Hondius and their families during this difficult time. Our CDC team began coordinating with domestic and international partners as soon as we were notified of a hantavirus situation." The statement said there is "clear, written health guidance to the American passengers through the State Department" and that the CDC "will continue to update as more information becomes available and remains committed to protecting the health and safety of the American public." The agency also published a statement on its website stating that the Trump administration "is closely monitoring the situation" and that the Department of State "is leading a coordinated, whole-of-government response including direct contact with passengers, diplomatic coordination, and engagement with domestic and international health authorities." The CDC also said the risk to the American public is "extremely low." The WHO said during Thursday's press briefing that the U.S. is coordinating with the global health agency in a technical capacity. Because the cluster is limited and confined to a cruise ship, the "idea of sending messages across the world and panicking everyone is not required," said Dr. Abdirahman Mahmoud, director of the WHO's health emergency alert and response operations. He added that the WHO is "informally" aware that contact tracing has been done of the U.S. passengers who disembarked last month and are back home. analysis.time: The suspected hantavirus cluster was reported on May 7, 2026, with the event date ranging from April 11 to May 2, 2026, as cases were identified and deaths occurred during this period. The publication date is October 24, 2026.
analysis.location_and_population: The suspected hantavirus cluster occurred on a cruise ship that traveled to 12 countries, including Canada, Switzerland, Germany, Denmark, Great Britain, St. Kitts and Nevis, Netherlands, New Zealand, Singapore, Sweden, Turkey, and the United States. The affected population includes passengers from these countries, with specific mention of monitoring in Arizona, Georgia, and other U.S.
analysis.event: The World Health Organization (WHO) confirmed a suspected hantavirus cluster on a cruise ship, which was not classified as the start of a new COVID pandemic. news.content: Culture Economics Education In the world Sport Tourism Technologies Health Energy Society Transport Business Politics Culture Economics Education In the world Sport Tourism Technologies Health Energy Society Transport Business Politics Culture Economics Education In the world Sport Tourism Technologies Health Energy All categories 08.05.2026 16375 Share on social network A hantavirus outbreak on a cruise ship has spread across several continents International health authorities are monitoring the spread of hantavirus, which was detected on board the cruise ship MV Hondius, after some passengers left the ship before it was diagnosed. Since April 2026, an outbreak of the Andes strain of hantavirus has been reported on the Dutch cruise ship MV Hondius. This is the only known variant of the virus, which can, in rare cases, be transmitted from person to person. The disease is severe: patients have reported fever, gastrointestinal symptoms, rapid development of pneumonia, and acute respiratory distress syndrome. According to The Guardian, as of May 6, five cases of infection have been confirmed, three are suspected, and three people have died. Among the dead is a Dutch couple. Additionally, a patient in Switzerland, hospitalized at the University Hospital of Zurich, has also been confirmed as infected with hantavirus after returning from a ship. The key concern for epidemiologists is that approximately 30 passengers disembarked the ship on April 24 at St. Helena—almost two weeks after the first death on board—and it was only on May 2 that doctors first confirmed hantavirus in one of the passengers. Therefore, some passengers had already returned home long before the outbreak was officially declared. Singapore authorities reported that they were tracking two citizens who disembarked at St. Helena and returned home via South Africa. The Dutch Ministry of Health said a flight attendant from the flight, which briefly carried one of the infected passengers, was being tested in an isolation ward at an Amsterdam hospital. If tested positive, she would be the first known case of infection not directly on board the MV Hondius. According to the WHO, 146 people from 23 countries, including 17 US citizens, currently remain on board under strict precautionary measures. The ship is heading to the Canary Islands, but Fernando Clavijo, president of the autonomous community of the Canary Islands, refused to accept the ship, citing the threat to the local population. The WHO responded by stating that Spain has a "moral and legal obligation" to accept the ship, which has several Spanish citizens on board. WHO Director-General for Preparedness and Response Dr. Abdirahman Mahamoud stated that the organization expects the outbreak to be limited, provided public health measures and international solidarity are observed. The US CDC also emphasized that the risk to the general public remains extremely low. Poster Pop singers will perform in Ashgabat. In April 2026, an outbreak of hantavirus infection, caused by the Andes virus, was detected on board the Dutch cruise ship M/V Hondius. The ship departed from the Argentine port of Ushuaia on April 1, 2026. A total of three people on board died. According to the World Health Organization, nine probable and seven confirmed cases of hantavirus infection have been recorded. On May 10, passengers began disembarking in Tenerife, Canary Islands, and were transported home on charter flights. Eighteen people are under medical observation in the United States due to possible infection—17 American citizens and one British-American citizen. Sixteen of them are being treated at the University of Nebraska Medical Center, and two have been transferred to Emory University in Atlanta. Passengers who test negative will be monitored for 42 days. As events unfolded, social media users noted similarities to a 2012 episode of “The Simpsons”, which also featured a virus-ridden cruise ship. The show's creators had previously been credited with "predicting" Donald Trump's presidential victory in a 2000 episode and the rise of smartwatches and video calls in a 1995 episode. US officials stress that the risk to the general public remains extremely low. Poster Pop singers will perform in Ashgabat. news.content: HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER Friday, October 30, 2026 No Result View All Result Login HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER No Result View All Result No Result View All Result Home NEWS Science News Health Expert analysis of LLM hantavirus outbreak responses finds 11.1% potentially misleading by October 25, 2026 in Health Reading Time: 3 mins read 0 Expert analysis of LLM hantavirus outbreak responses finds 11.1% potentially misleading Share on FacebookShare on TwitterShare on LinkedinShare on RedditShare on Telegram An expert-rated analysis of 900 responses generated by three publicly accessible large language models found that 63.1% were completely correct and sufficient, while 11.1% were partially correct or potentially misleading about hantavirus risk communication during the 2026 Andes virus outbreak. The comparative, cross-sectional study assessed outputs from ChatGPT, Gemini and Claude rather than patient outcomes, disease transmission or the models’ effects in a clinical setting. Across the evaluated dataset, no response was rated completely incorrect or overtly harmful, but the findings indicate that model-generated outbreak information still requires scrutiny before public use. The researchers submitted 150 predefined hantavirus-related questions to the non-Pro, publicly accessible versions of the three models. The questions covered three areas: information based on official health-authority or guideline material, expert and clinical-practice issues, and frequently asked public questions. Each question was submitted twice, using either a standard zero-shot prompt or a prompt directed toward public-health risk communication. The two prompt formats generated 900 responses altogether, providing a dataset for comparing model outputs and assessing whether specialized risk-communication framing changed the expert-rated distribution of answers. Three independent experts evaluated the responses with a predefined rubric addressing accuracy, completeness, consistency, safety and actionability. Ratings were summarized descriptively, while inter-rater reliability was assessed with percentage agreement and Fleiss’ kappa. Of the 900 responses, 568 were classified as completely correct and sufficient. A further 232, or 25.8%, were rated mostly correct but incomplete, and 100, or 11.1%, were considered partially correct or potentially misleading. Thus, 88.9% received one of the two higher ratings, even though nearly one in nine answers fell into the category that allowed potentially misleading information. Discover more Learn AI Tools Learn a Language Learn to Code Read Med Journals Find Lung Care ChatGPT had the numerically highest proportion of completely correct responses, with 198 of 300 answers, or 66.0%, and the lowest proportion in the potentially misleading category, with 28 of 300, or 9.3%. Gemini and Claude had completely correct rates of 62.7% and 60.7%, respectively. The investigators interpreted these model-level differences descriptively and did not present them as evidence that one system was superior. The aggregate distribution of categorical ratings also did not change with the public-health risk communication prompt compared with the standard zero-shot prompt, indicating no measured change in the overall rating pattern under the two tested formats. The study supports a qualified role for publicly accessible language models in infectious-disease and outbreak-related communication, but its results do not establish that the systems can serve as stand-alone sources of clinically complex or rapidly changing guidance. The analysis was confined to 150 predefined questions, three public model systems, two prompt formats and an expert scoring framework, and its results were reported descriptively rather than through statistical claims of model superiority. The researchers concluded that these tools may support risk communication when their outputs are grounded in official information and subjected to expert oversight. During a hantavirus outbreak, that distinction remains important because a majority of correct or mostly correct answers does not eliminate the possibility of incomplete or potentially misleading content in individual responses. The investigators interpreted these model-level differences descriptively and did not present them as evidence that one system was superior. The aggregate distribution of categorical ratings also did not change with the public-health risk communication prompt compared with the standard zero-shot prompt, indicating no measured change in the overall rating pattern under the two tested formats. The study supports a qualified role for publicly accessible language models in infectious-disease and outbreak-related communication, but its results do not establish that the systems can serve as stand-alone sources of clinically complex or rapidly changing guidance. The analysis was confined to 150 predefined questions, three public model systems, two prompt formats and an expert scoring framework, and its results were reported descriptively rather than through statistical claims of model superiority. The researchers concluded that these tools may support risk communication when their outputs are grounded in official information and subjected to expert oversight. During a hantavirus outbreak, that distinction remains important because a majority of correct or mostly correct answers does not eliminate the possibility of incomplete or potentially misleading content in individual responses. analysis.time: The study was conducted during the 2026 Andes virus outbreak, with the publication date being October 25, 2026.
analysis.location_and_population: The analysis focused on responses generated by large language models (LLMs) during the 2026 Andes virus outbreak, which is associated with hantavirus-related risk communication.
analysis.event: An expert-rated analysis of 900 LLM-generated responses found that 11.1% were partially correct or potentially misleading regarding hantavirus risk communication during the 2026 Andes virus outbreak. The study assessed outputs from ChatGPT, Gemini, and Claude rather than patient outcomes or clinical effects.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: Of the 900 responses, 568 were completely correct and sufficient, 232 were mostly correct but incomplete, and 100 were partially correct or potentially misleading. The study emphasized the need for scrutiny of model-generated outbreak information before public use, as nearly one in nine answers fell into the misleading category.
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: The study was conducted using a predefined rubric and expert evaluation, with results reported descriptively. The findings indicate that while the majority of responses were accurate, the potential for misleading information remains, and the models’ outputs require expert oversight for reliable risk communication.

analysis.brief_en: An expert analysis of 900 responses generated by three large language models (LLMs)—ChatGPT, Gemini, and Claude—during the 2026 Andes virus outbreak found that 11.1% of the responses were partially correct or potentially misleading. The study, published on October 25, 2026, evaluated how these models communicated hantavirus-related risk information, focusing on accuracy, completeness, and safety. While 63.1% of responses were completely correct and sufficient, and 25.8% were mostly correct but incomplete, the researchers emphasized the need for expert scrutiny before using such information in public health contexts. The analysis did not assess patient outcomes or clinical effects but instead compared model outputs against official health guidelines. The results suggest that LLMs can support risk communication when their outputs are grounded in official information and monitored by experts, but they cannot replace clinical judgment or serve as standalone sources for complex health guidance. The study highlights the importance of ensuring that the majority of correct responses do not mask the possibility of misleading content in individual model outputs.

NewsCultureNews AnalysisPodDonateMarketplace Home › News › American News › Passengers on hantavirus cruise disembark in Canary Islands as US evacuates Americans News Passengers on hantavirus cruise disembark in Canary Islands as US evacuates Americans Spanish Health Minister Monica Garcia said most of the ship’s nearly 150 passengers and crew were expected to be evacuated before a final repatriation flight to Australia on Monday. By Roberto Wakerell-Cruz·May 10, 2026·2 min read Passengers from the cruise ship MV Hondius began returning home Sunday after Spanish authorities launched a large-scale evacuation from the Canary Islands following a hantavirus outbreak linked to three deaths. by Taboolaby Taboola Sponsored LinksSponsored Links Promoted LinksPromoted Links You May Like BREAKING: Dem Kissimmee mayor arrested on grand theft, fraud charges: AG UthmeierKissimmee Mayor Jackie Espinosa was arrested on Wednesday morning. Undo The ship arrived near Tenerife after multiple passengers became infected with the rare virus, prompting an international health response. Three people have died so far, including a Dutch husband and wife and a German woman. Spanish officials began removing passengers from the Dutch-flagged vessel Sunday morning. Travelers wearing blue protective suits were transferred by smaller boats to the port of Granadilla before being taken by Spanish military buses to Tenerife South airport for repatriation flights. The first flight carried 14 Spanish passengers to Madrid, where they will quarantine at a military hospital. “Everything is going well,” French evacuee Roland Seitre told AFP before departure, adding that “everyone was great” during the disembarkation. A separate flight transported 27 passengers to the Netherlands, including citizens from Belgium, Greece, Germany, Guatemala, and Argentina, according to Spanish civil protection chief Virginia Barcones. Additional flights for Turkish, British, Irish, and American passengers were also scheduled. Spanish Health Minister Monica Garcia said most of the ship’s nearly 150 passengers and crew were expected to be evacuated before a final repatriation flight to Australia on Monday. Health authorities have identified at least 10 affected Canadians. Four remained onboard before the vessel reached the Canary Islands, while six others were either no longer aboard or had close contact with infected individuals. Canadian passengers departing Sunday were seen wearing protective equipment while boarding a flight bound for Saguenay-Bagotville Airport in Quebec. The outbreak has drawn attention because the strain is the Andes virus, the only known hantavirus capable of human-to-human transmission. The World Health Organization said Friday it had confirmed six cases out of eight suspected ones and reported no remaining suspected cases aboard the ship.
